in writing. − it is certainly right and important to set clear rules for rating agencies and to implement them accordingly. especially when you consider that the market is dominated by three large us companies that hold around 90 percent of the market share. however, and this is a misunderstanding by some members whose countries are affected by poor ratings, market participants and investors need to have a more or less independent assessment in order to assess the risk of any investment. it may be true that in the years before the crisis, rating agencies were blind to the various derivatives and wrongly assigned good ratings to the toxic papers. nevertheless, the downgrades of various european debtor states over the past three years have been justified. these countries not only have a short-term liquidity problem, but are structurally deficitary and heavily indebted. the credit rating agencies cannot be blamed for drawing attention to this fact now, especially in the light of the criticism they have received in connection with the crisis. i cannot therefore endorse the ideas of 'punishing' the agencies in various ways as expressed in this report, which is why i abstained.
in writing. - i voted for the amendment of the regulation on credit rating agencies, as the report contains good approaches to better control and transparency. credit rating agencies have an enormous influence on our economic system. they assess the creditworthiness of governments and companies, which in turn determines their creditworthiness. a single assessment can thus affect the lives of many european citizens. in recent years, it has become clear that credit rating agencies have unnecessarily fuelled the economic and financial crisis. more control is urgently needed: the report commits credit rating agencies to greater transparency, for example on ownership structure and disclosure obligations. the country ratings need to be reviewed more frequently. these are important measures, but i do not think they go far enough. the three largest agencies still hold a 90% market share. the commission has already taken a number of initiatives to improve the quality of the information provided by the european rating agency. credit rating agencies must be able to be held accountable for negligent mis-ratings.
in writing. − in the background of the financial crisis the credit rating agencies regulation has been a topic on which the council and the parliament agreed on new rules which are being applied now at eu level. these rules concentrate on a common regulation for the issuance of the credit ratings. this meaning that cras need to apply for registration and adhere to the rules that ensure a high quality of ratings. applying this new regulation the cras are more transparent. i voted in favour of the report as it simplifies the cras procedure.
in writing. − the highly controversial role that credit rating agencies have played and continue to play in the ongoing financial and economic crisis highlights not only the importance of credit risk assessments and valuations in financial markets, but also the devastating financial consequences that these assessments can have. we should also be reminded that the usa, despite its massive public debt and its continuous internal disputes, continues to receive top marks, while eu countries have already been massively downgraded in their credit rating under similar circumstances. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. i have taken these considerations into account in my voting behaviour.
in writing. − in the fight against global overfishing, we have repeatedly set time limits at eu level for fishing with certain gear and in certain sea areas. at the same time, it is virtually impossible to control compliance with these provisions. this will not be affected by changes in the fan quotas after adjustment of the minimum fishing mortality values in accordance with scientific advice. i think that the consumer problem is similar to the shark fin problem. i voted in that direction.
in writing. − a regionalised approach to stock management, based on technical measures for the conservation of fishery resources, which establishes rules on fishing areas and gear but not fishing quotas, may be an important part of conservation provisions. the problem, as always, is implementation. that is why i abstained in the vote.
in writing. - article 13 (1) of the rules of procedure provides that, in the event of an equal number of candidates and vacancies, the president may call an election by teleconference or by secret ballot in accordance with rule 169. in the case of an election by popular vote, the president would have to decide at the same time on the order of precedence of the vice-presidents (article 15 (2), second subparagraph). concern was expressed that such a determination by the president might not be unanimously agreed in some cases. if the political groups agree on the persons to be nominated, these persons (usually 14) are elected by a roll-call vote. the ranking is then determined by a vote. the reason for this is that the groups may agree on the persons but not on the order of precedence. in such a situation, the president waives the right (legally vested in him) to determine the order of precedence. if the political groups do not agree on the persons to be elected or if 'independent' candidates stand for election, a vote shall be taken and the order of precedence shall be determined by the order in which the candidates were elected. i think these proposals are sensible and that is why i voted for the amendment of the rules of procedure.
in writing. − a change in the rules of procedure is to be welcomed, particularly if it facilitates the establishment of consensus and increases the opportunities for stakeholders to have a say in a reasonable way.
in writing. the importance of the introduction of a youth guarantee throughout europe cannot be denied: the financial and economic crisis, coupled with unilateral austerity programmes, has led to an explosion in unemployment. with youth unemployment rates of over 50% in spain or greece, we are in danger of losing a whole generation of young europeans. instead of dragging these countries deeper into recession through austerity, there is a need for solidarity at european level in support of active labour market policies, for example programmes such as the youth guarantee. in austria, this project has already been successfully implemented. the training guarantee for young people, combined with the extension of apprenticeship training, has led to an immediate relaxation of the apprenticeship market and a significant reduction in youth unemployment. this is exactly the kind of project europe needs now. we must act quickly: across the continent, youth unemployment is rising faster than total unemployment. the urgency of the situation must also be taken into account in the considerations for the negotiations on the multiannual financial framework.
in writing. − currently, one in four young people in europe is unemployed. if we take a more detailed look at the current situation, we find a youth unemployment rate of 40 — 50 % in some member states. the phrase ‘lost generation’ has become pure reality. to ensure this situation does not get even worse, urgent and immediate action is of utmost priority. with this ‘youth guarantee’, young people should be able to find a job more quickly (within four months) after completing their education or, if unemployed, receive a job offer. this is a first step to help and support the young unemployed. that is why i voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. − the treaty of lisbon gave european energy policy its own legal basis in primary law for the first time. this means that the objectives of 'security of supply' and 'economy of energy supply' can now also be pursued explicitly. the eu's energy strategy is geared towards achieving three objectives in the long term. the eu wants to tackle climate change, reduce the eu's external vulnerability due to its high dependence on fossil fuels, and promote growth and jobs through a competitive energy supply. looking at the eu's overall energy mix, fossil fuels continue to account for the largest shares of the total: oil (36.9%), gas (24%) and coal (17.8%). nuclear energy accounts for 14% and renewable energy for 7.1%. the import dependence is already very high for crude oil at 84% and for natural gas at 61%. i voted against the report because i believe that the individual member states should take greater care to ensure that energy is supplied autonomously. this would not only have the great advantage of eliminating dependence on fossil fuels from crisis regions, but would also be the best way to protect the climate, since many member states, such as austria, can only do so if they rely more on renewable energy.
in writing. - the rapporteur presents a very broad overall approach which takes account of both economic and social factors. the needs of individual countries and citizens are taken into account as well as the requirements of environmental policies and the economy. the emphasis on renewable energy, the adaptation of energy to the needs of individual regions and the well-considered financial approaches to support and cooperation between the union, member states and third countries are noteworthy.

in writing. - the introduction of eurobonds or eurobills is a major decision. the debt of individuals is being transferred to all the states. the interest rate on government bonds is an important indicator for investors of the risk of an investment. the higher the ratio, the higher the risk of failure for investors. conversely, however, the interest rate also limits the amount of debt borne by debtor countries. it is therefore a natural and reasonable regulatory instrument which can be influenced by the states themselves. a good businessman gets a lower interest rate and can borrow more money. the euro has thrown this important principle overboard, and by aligning interest rates across europe, it has ensured that the crisis countries have borrowed disproportionately and far beyond their means. the result is known. greece is bankrupt, cyprus, portugal and spain are close to it. so, despite this recognition, those who still support eurobonds, which are misusedly called 'stability bonds', either have not understood the situation or deliberately want the taxpayers of the solvent countries to pay for debts that they did not create or that are not their concern. that's incredible, which is why i couldn't resist this paper.
in writing. the report on the feasibility of introducing stability bonds sets out a realistic roadmap for the introduction of such bonds at european level. eurobonds are a controversial subject, but i believe they can make a significant contribution to combating the financial and economic crisis. debt relief by crisis-hit countries can only be possible if moderate interest rates are available.
in writing. − eurobonds are considered as a regulatory instrument of the euro area. stability bonds should, inter alia, ensure the sustainability of the budgetary position of the member states and provide liquid assets for investors. the introduction of eurobonds, however, risks alienating investors from national debt. the introduction of eurobonds would not, in my view, lead to the stabilisation of the eurozone. it would only lead to further distortions of the market. as 'eu presidency', we must take action to eliminate market instability and distortions. i have also said that i am not going to vote for the report because i believe that the national budgets are still in serious deficit and that the measures taken so far have not been successful or that some member states are not making the necessary efforts.

the commission has already made a number of proposals. we all agree in this house that small and mediumsized enterprises are the economic backbone of the european union. more than 99% of all enterprises are smes. they create 85% of all new jobs and they are the number one taxpayer among businesses. the financing of smes is therefore closely linked to the ability to invest, competitiveness, growth and employment on our continent. we have a phenomenon which is different: 80% of the financing of smes is financed by credit. smes are therefore highly dependent on credit. we must do everything possible to increase the supply of capital, to increase opportunities, to facilitate access to the capital market, and we are trying to ensure that the retail limit for private loans is raised by 50% to 1.5 million in the basel iii and crd iv banking regulations, and we are trying to reduce the risk weight for sme loans by 30%, because sme loans do not represent an increased risk, but are a necessity for growth and employment on this continent. we need to ensure that eu funds million go directly to businesses and that the heterogeneity of sme activity is respected. a broader funding base is therefore urgently needed.
in writing. while the credit crunch affects small and large enterprises alike, smes have traditionally lower equity capital than larger enterprises and, owing to high information and transaction costs, have limited access to external sources of finance. this makes bank loans the most important external source of finance for smes. we know that the financing conditions for investment have deteriorated massively since 2009. this is reflected in the increased collateral requirements, higher interest charges and higher documentation requirements. in addition, suppliers are more restrictive in their handling of supplier loans, and they are also faced with limit reductions by their credit insurers. so we need not be surprised by the increasing rate of sme insolvency. in this tense situation, it is all the more shameful that all sme initiatives at eu level are mainly on paper. it is long overdue that access to eu funding for smes is finally made easier. and it is precisely in the tense times of the financial crisis and the euribor scandals that the timely implementation of the new basel rules must be constantly reviewed, especially when the us, which exerts the greatest pressure here, is constantly lagging behind.

in writing. − the lisbon treaty has confirmed that the outermost regions are characterised by their great distance from the community's internal market and by persistent disadvantages which give them a unique special position within the eu, which justifies the implementation of appropriate measures. agriculture is a strategic economic sector in the outermost regions in two ways. on the one hand, it is one of the main sources of employment and economic development in these regions, and a large proportion of the working population is connected to it. on the other hand, agriculture and its diversification have a link with the concept of food security, which is all the more important for these regions, which are isolated regions on islands and far from the european mainland. the increase in the food self-sufficiency rate, which must lead to a reduction in imports of agricultural products and, at the same time, to an increase in the volume and types of own agricultural products, is of enormous importance for the outermost regions and their development strategies. that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - this report deals with specific measures in the field of agriculture for the benefit of the outermost regions of the union; this includes overseas regions in portugal, spain and france. the posei programme is indispensable for the agricultural production and processing industries in these regions. without this programme, viability could be threatened by the economic difficulties of the geographical situation. the posei programmes are divided into two different schemes, the supply scheme and the measures for local production, which account for about 80% of total assistance. the posei programmes - special supply arrangements and measures to assist local production - do not require any substantial changes. the financial allocation totalling eur 653 million for the nine regions is insufficient due to the declining share of agriculture in total economic activity. the competitiveness of imports from third countries is also not favourable. sustainable methods should also be applied and the eu should be more vigilant in controlling imports from third countries to avoid unfair competition with local products.

i would like to thank the commissioner for his reply. companies are part of society, so they also have a responsibility to society. they create jobs and are the engines of the european economy. as my colleague richard howitt's report makes clear, the external exercise of social responsibility is an indispensable condition for credibly correcting the mistakes of the past and restoring lost confidence in europe's economy. the report by my colleague baldassarre makes it clear that by increasing transparency and by integrating csr into the core policies of european companies, negative impacts of corporate activities on businesses can be identified, cushioned and possibly - and above all hopefully - avoided. fair wages, good social security for employees and high health standards are among them. only by taking account of the social contribution of enterprises to society can there ever be a sustained and not just short-term recovery of the european economy. the two reports before us make parliament's position on the csr strategy quite clear. we are calling for greater transparency and disclosure, not just financial disclosure, but also for you, commissioner, to legislate on reporting on compliance with social and environmental standards. it is also important to me to make it clear that european companies also bear some responsibility for the behaviour of their subcontractors. if all companies had to disclose their production standards, it would create a much greater public pressure to force the big players in the industries to adhere to ilo standards and thus create a better and fairer world.
the commission has already done so. i understand the social responsibility of enterprises, as the commission has already said, as part of the framework of values with which we want to create a sustainable economic system in europe. this includes competitiveness, as my colleague mr baldassarre's report very precisely shows. i would like to add my support to the words of thomas mann and also to those of mrs hirsch, who have spelled out the value of voluntary action and the disadvantages of regulation to the point of over-regulation. we are in a situation where i think we want to ensure that the new rules do not impose constraints, especially on small and mediumsized enterprises, because they can endanger the economic security of these enterprises. it simply involves protection against excessive administrative burdens. it is the small and mediumsized enterprises in particular which demonstrate their social responsibility: to their employees, to their environment and to society. and that is to be preserved. the commission has submitted a report to us, and from that we, as the european parliament, have defined social responsibility in both reports. i am also looking forward with great anticipation to the commissioner's report in a few weeks' time.

in writing. the customs union of the european union was extended by the accession of bulgaria and romania. therefore, there is an obligation under wto law to enter into negotiations with wto member states to compensate for the increase in the captive duty rates and the resulting losses. in order to compensate for a deterioration in trade position, the duty-free tariff quotas for certain products from the usa are being increased. i therefore vote in favour of this compensatory agreement because it shows that the eu is committed to a trading system based on multilateral rules.
in writing. − on paper, it may sound good that the eu is urging its member states to continue to make every effort in the following priority areas: increasing labour force participation and reducing structural unemployment; building a skilled workforce potential and promoting job quality and lifelong learning; promoting social inclusion and combating poverty. in practice, member states themselves have been working towards these objectives long before they were set by the eu. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. i rejected the report in protest against this project of centralisation in brussels.
in writing. - the stubborn attitude of many representatives of the european institutions to want to direct the economic policy of the whole of europe from a central position is not in line with historical experience. the state as the driver of an entire economy, particularly in the form of the eu as a super-agency, negates the need for economic policies that are sometimes very different from one region to another. it also ignores the lack of capacity of the state. the role of the state is to provide an important framework and to provide incentives. the mainly inefficient financing programmes through the european social fund lead at best to efficient employment programmes in the short term, but cannot replace the employment effects of an economy. the eu also wants to promote the pooling of national competences at european level. i therefore consider that the report cannot be supported.
in writing. − a comprehensive and active labour market policy is an important part of a successful economic policy. this applies both to individual countries and even more so to the member states of the european union. the main objective of employment policy must be to combat unemployment. in the current situation, the main focus is on combating youth unemployment, but also on providing greater support for older workers. at the same time, the quality of work and adequate pay must be maintained. the coordination of the various member states is of the utmost importance. that is why i voted for the report. the principle of 'equal pay for equal work at the same place' must always be taken into account.
in writing. − the directive on the pricing of medicinal products for human use should bring up to date outdated transparency requirements for all measures for the pricing and reimbursement of medicinal products in the member states, without prejudice to their responsibility for public health and financing. it also provided for the price of medicines to be the same throughout the eu and for the authorisation procedures to be harmonised. the idea is that the internal market for medicinal products should be fully open and that there should be equal opportunities in the market. i did not vote for the report because i believe that each member state should continue to have the right to decide for itself, particularly as regards the authorization of medicinal products, the criteria on which a medicinal product is authorized. since the rules differ from country to country, they should also be able to decide on the date of authorisation.
in writing. − the aim of the common fisheries policy is to ensure that fisheries and aquaculture are conducted in a long-term, sustainable and ecological manner and that food supplies are guaranteed. i've been working to ensure that all the fish caught are kept on board and eventually landed. the proposal is to introduce an absolute ban on discards, to be phased in from 2014 onwards, according to a timetable that will be specific to each species. in doing so, member states are obliged to ensure that the ban on discarding on board fishing vessels is respected. the objective is to return fish stocks to levels that can produce the maximum sustainable yield by 2015 at the latest and by 2020 at the latest. in order to ensure sustainability and planning certainty, long-term plans should also regulate the management of fish stocks.
in writing. − although the new basic regulation is intended to provide an ambitious basis for solving long-standing problems (overfishing, overcapacity, the poor economic situation of many enterprises in the fisheries sector, social problems due to the decline of fisheries in many coastal regions), it is unlikely to be more successful than the previous regulation. although it is of course important that the eu sets a good example in this respect. it would be useful to try first to work on a better implementation of the measures taken so far. nevertheless, i voted in favour of this report because the union should set a good example in this area.
in writing. - the keyword in this vote is sustainability. the current fisheries policy sought to maximise short-term profits and resulted in serious overfishing. but it is not only necessary to stop overfishing, but also to increase the stock. in this way the mistakes and greed of the past can be made good. the commission has also adopted a proposal for a regulation on the conservation of fishery resources in the north sea. this wasteful and unnecessary death of many fish has been an accepted collateral damage. this too is now being significantly counteracted.
in writing. − it must be noted that some of the ideas presented here are worthy of support and should be pushed forward. electrically powered vehicles and hybrid vehicles have been heavily promoted in recent years. however, their almost silent propulsion can be dangerous to people with hearing impairments. the engine noise of other vehicles alerts pedestrians, cyclists and other road users to an approaching danger, especially, of course, those who are visually impaired or blind. for them, the noise of vehicles is essential to survive road traffic without being harmed. the introduction of an acoustic warning tone for such vehicles or artificial engine noise seems appropriate to maintain road safety. the desire to reduce traffic noise overall is understandable. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's environmental policy is not distorted by the introduction of new technologies. it seems more sensible to force the road to be quieter. i have abstained because of the immaturity of the whole proposal.
in writing. the current economic crisis is affecting the member states of the european union in different ways, as is the case with migration flows and the immense costs associated with them. it is in the interest of all member states to ensure that the flow of migrants from outside europe is managed efficiently, even in the context of the crisis. the southern european countries, particularly those which have been particularly weakened by the economic crisis, are now also having to cope with the continuing flows of refugees from north africa and the arab world. there is a real danger that immigration controls will collapse due to acute financial constraints in individual countries. that is why i am in favour of increasing the funding of the european refugee fund and the european fund for the integration of third-country nationals.

would like to thank him. the creation of a true and effective area of freedom and justice in europe cannot be completed without the introduction of a deep judicial culture based on mutual trust within the different national systems. there has been a fundamental change in parliament’s approach towards judicial training in this legislature. this is also due to parliament’s strong and forward-looking position and, in particular, to the reflections hosted by the committee on legal affairs in this house. the entry into force of the lisbon treaty and the objectives set down in the stockholm programme have paved the way for a substantial increase in the level of european union activity in the field of judicial cooperation. the stockholm programme outlines in particular the importance of strengthening the establishment of a truly european judicial culture which fully respects the principles of subsidiarity and judicial independence. this is also one of the top priorities for policy in the area of freedom, security and justice and therefore for parliament’s committee on legal affairs. this is a top priority of the socialist group in the area of freedom, security and justice. over the coming years, member states will in fact be called upon to implement existing legislative and non-legislative instruments in this field, as well as to participate in the adoption of new instruments. however, this increased law-making activity must proceed in parallel with a harmonious and effective practical application of these tools. in this respect, the role of the members of the judiciary and judicial staff becomes crucial. european judicial training should therefore take a new shape and dimension. the idea behind this, which parliament has tried to promote during the last two years with its numerous resolutions, is to promote a bottom-up approach. this will involve member states’ national associations of legal professionals, such as lawyers, judges and universities, in compliance with the principle of subsidiarity. we therefore welcome the experience in the netherlands with eurinfra and its network of court coordinators for european law, which has been emulated by other member states, in particular italy, with its european gaius project, denmark, romania and bulgaria. those experiences are designed around three pillars: improving the accessibility of european law information resources using web technology, improving knowledge of european law among the judiciary, and establishing and maintaining a network of court coordinators for european law. there is no excuse today for ignorance of european law. national judges are, and must be, european judges, called upon to play a fundamental role in a situation in which we will need more europe. this does not preclude fostering a european judicial culture in which diversity is celebrated as a common good. we should promote the idea of national court coordinators with european law and their interconnection at european level. in particular the main function of an interconnected network of court coordinators would be to enable judges to readily confer on their day-to-day work with their counterparts in other member states on matters such as the interpretation of the applicable european law in a secure, digital environment. these circles of coherence would make for greater uniformity in the application of european union law, while reducing the number of references for preliminary rulings, without detracting from the role of the court of justice. in developing such search engines for searching judgments, opinions and european union law in general, member states should consider whether this technology might not benefit the judiciary in other member states as well, in which case technology can be pooled, coordinated and developed in common. finally i would just like to thank mr zwiefka for his good cooperation and also for the support in the group in the committee on legal in writing. − the european union is facing a significant ageing population. in 2060 there will be only two people of working age for every person over 65; today, the ratio is 1 to 4. in addition, the population aged over 65 will almost double between 2008 and 2060. in figures, this means that some 151 million people will be over 65 years of age. the older generation could become a major burden on the working population, but still be so active that their living space and social utility need to be adapted. there is a growing demographic change that needs to be addressed. however, the labour market will also have to change, as active ageing will be expected to lead to an increase in the retirement age if society is to continue to meet the generational contract. i did not vote for the report because it is doubtful whether an artificial change in the social structure and the environment will actually make life more pleasant for the elderly. the report does not indicate whether the opposite might be true, namely that the elderly would be overburdened.

in writing. - the proposals for the harmonisation of accounting standards mentioned by the rapporteur are very welcome, as they will make the management of greenhouse gas emissions and their reduction more transparent and fair. the implementation of land use, land use change and forestry management is a step in the right direction towards effective eu-wide emission reduction regimes.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'common carrier' in the definition of the term 'common carrier'. this is in addition to the specificisation of existing agreements, and takes into account the new unfccc commitments to provide financial and technological assistance to developing countries. the collection, analysis and provision of sufficient and comprehensive data on greenhouse gas emissions is an important basis for addressing climate change.
in writing. − in principle, it may be a good idea to set up a free interactive website in all the eu's official languages as a single point of contact for consumers and businesses to resolve out-of-court contractual disputes. this voluntary system will not, however, be sufficient to improve consumer protection in a sustainable way. i voted in that direction.
in writing. − the regulation on the online settlement of consumer disputes is an important step towards strengthening legal certainty for consumers. more and more people are making online purchases, and often these are cross-border. in disputes with dealers that may arise from such purchases, customers usually take the short cut. this is why it is necessary to provide consumers with an opportunity to access and obtain information on out-of-court dispute settlement online. the regulation creates a european platform for precisely such cases.
in writing. − the introduction of an online dispute resolution platform is highly desirable in times of strong growth in cross-border online sales of goods and online provision of services. the system is particularly positive in that it applies to both consumers and businesses. it makes an important contribution to a europe of free movement of goods and facilitates access through its free access and availability in all official languages.
in writing. − the present proposal aims to create a simple, convenient and cost-effective means of settling disputes relating to the sale of goods or the provision of services within the eu. this voluntary system is in principle to be welcomed, but it will not be sufficient to improve the legal protection of consumers in a lasting way. i voted in that direction.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on alternative forms of consumer dispute settlement, as the entry into force of the legislative initiative will strengthen the rights of consumers. this will enable all citizens to resolve disputes about purchases quickly and inexpensively. the fact is that consumers are afraid of lengthy and costly legal proceedings and are thus denied their rights. the out-of-court settlement of disputes can counteract this and thus strengthen the autonomy of consumers.
in writing. - in any case, it is important to promote the protection of consumer rights and to strengthen their position. the expansion of adr entities described in this report, as well as the improvement of their infrastructure and awareness, will make an important contribution to helping consumers enforce their rights. alternatives to the judicial process in dispute settlement are often desirable for all for cost reasons and should be supported accordingly.
in writing. − the european countries and territories in the atlantic, caribbean and pacific are outposts of european culture and values in the world and, because of their special geographical location, offer important economic and political opportunities for the union. the new association decision is essential for the union's continued positive cooperation with the overseas regions of europe, as the old agreement of 2001 will expire at the end of this year. in order to continue the positive cooperation with these areas and to put them on a new legal basis, i support the motion for a resolution.
in writing. − the report is very positive, as it is well researched and relevant to the eu, alongside sound reasoning. the overseas countries and territories play a crucial role in the eu, as they are 'external bases' for dealing with issues of interest to the eu (such as globalisation or international trade). the octs also have natural resources and a range of options which make them innovative actors in international negotiations. nevertheless, the octs must continue to be supported.
in writing. - i supported this motion to guarantee the safety and health of the citizens of the european union. in view of the negative experience of the past and the fact that states and companies have repeatedly attempted to cover up radioactive incidents, it seems appropriate to set low limits for ionising radiation in order to detect and respond to potential contamination at an early stage. clean drinking water and free access to it is a fundamental right of our citizens which cannot be restricted, and it is the duty of the authorities to ensure that it remains so.
in writing. - the rules of the so-called 'two-pack' severely restrict the capacity of nation states to act and are totally unacceptable. the budgetary rights of parliament are being cut and hollowed out so massively. but this is one of the most important rights of democratically legitimised national parliaments. the eu institutions suffer from a democratic deficit which has been somewhat reduced in recent times but which still persists. instead of increasingly sharing decisions and delegating powers to the eu, there is a need for the development and upgrading of the nation states in many areas. the fact that the framework conditions for national budgets are now dictated by the commission bureaucrats in brussels is unacceptable and that is why i voted against these proposals.
in writing. - i voted for the two-pack legislation because the current framework for stronger fiscal surveillance is no longer aimed at unilateral savings as originally planned by the commission, but contains more social rules for countries in crisis. we have seen that the current austerity policy is the wrong way forward and does not help the member states in crisis. in future, the eu commission will have to assess the social and economic impact of austerity measures on an economy. the troika will have to report to the eu parliament on the obligations imposed on crisis countries in future these rules will make budgetary control more democratic and transparent. the creation of a soli fund, a debt-repayment fund and the introduction of euro notes are other important objectives which will lead to greater solidarity within the euro area. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. as a trade unionist, i saw this as a central demand in the negotiations. the commission must not use the crisis as an excuse to reduce workers' rights! the procedures and institutions for wage formation must continue to be fully respected.
in writing. − the establishment of a system of targeted surveillance measures for member states threatened or affected by difficulties with respect to their financial stability is highly desirable, especially with a view to a strong and stable euro area, also after the financial and economic crisis.
in writing. − a comprehensive system for monitoring and assessing general government budgetary positions and ensuring the correction of excessive deficits in the euro area member states is desirable in order to help the european union overcome the financial and economic crisis and to promote a positive future development.
in writing. − the purpose of this proposal is to specify the criteria for the assets that a fund must meet in order to be designated as a 'european venture capital fund' and to obtain the corresponding passport. the creation of a european venture capital fund for smes is intended to counteract the massive increase in credit shortages since the banking crisis, which in my view is not in the cards, although it is questionable to what extent it can counteract the tightening of credit linked to the basle guidelines. i think it is more sensible to finally make it easier for smes to access eu funding and to speed up the long overdue reduction of bureaucracy.
in writing. - the above regulations and rules governing the nature, form, conduct and portfolio of the funds which may ultimately be described as 'european venture capital funds' seem to me to be appropriate. the requirements for transparency and investor confidence, the obligations and rights and the broadly defined behaviour between parties are also sufficient. i agree with this report because it contains a sufficient catalogue of criteria for the definition of european venture capital funds, which means that only suitable funds can be so designated.
in writing. − there is a growing interest among investors in social objectives, not just financial returns. this has created a market for social investment in europe (part of which is investment funds targeted at social enterprises). these funds finance social enterprises that drive social change through innovative solutions to social problems and make a valuable contribution to achieving the europe 2020 objectives by helping to address the social consequences of the financial crisis. the aim is to create a common framework for the use of the term 'european social entrepreneurship funds'. in particular, eu-wide rules govern the composition of the portfolio of funds and the categories of investors that can invest in such funds. the european council in brussels on 14 and 15 december adopted a resolution on the situation in the former yugoslavia. the removal of barriers is also intended to avoid distortions of competition.
in writing. − the economic crisis has had a profound impact on public budgets, the labour market and poverty. structural imbalances that women have already had to contend with are being exacerbated by the crisis: almost one third of all women in employment in the eu work part-time. they are more likely to be made redundant and often work unpaid. the current difficult situation on the labour market is pushing women even further into precarious and atypical employment relationships. public austerity and budget cuts also affect women more, because they are more likely than men to be employed in the sectors affected by austerity (health, education, etc.) and to be dependent on certain transfer services (e.g. provision of childcare facilities). the report also calls for the adoption of a new policy on the environment, which will be based on the principle of subsidiarity. policies, especially austerity measures, should be specifically analysed for gender implications and adapted accordingly.
in writing. − “as women we still ‘struggle’ on the labour market, as men we, sometimes, gain more than a woman for the same job.” in order to reduce gender inequalities at eu level but worldwide as well, to positively promote the image of the women in areas such as the labour market and jobs, education and culture, business promotion and economic growth, i voted in favour of the report. the gender pay gap, exacerbated by the financial crisis, the budgetary austerity policies (cuts in social security benefits) and all the other elements that still contribute to women falling into poverty have to be fought against.
in writing. - media and language convey images and therefore have a special social function. the media, which should be the ones to promote an enlightened image of women, are the ones that are doing the opposite: they are still too often conveying a traditional image of women. the report calls for important policy measures to combat stereotypes and sexism in the media. but here is another fundamental question: who sets the rules? i am firmly opposed to the concept of 'industrial voluntary commitment' as it is repeatedly pushed and demanded, mainly by industry representatives. i therefore support the motion to delete paragraph 14, which would give internet providers the power to rate content and, as a result, censor it. the industry is primarily driven by profit interests and has no democratic legitimacy. we, as members of the european parliament, should be particularly aware that the sovereign, the electorate, has entrusted us with the monopoly on 'lawmaking', and we should therefore resolutely resist attempts to undermine it. the commission has therefore decided to make a proposal to the council for a regulation on the application of the principle of equal treatment for men and women.
in writing. − to date, eu environmental policy has failed in many areas or has proved to be a toothless paper tiger. the commission has already taken a number of initiatives in this area. for example, the success of the trading of allowances, which by concealing aid does not reduce overall emissions but at best redistributes them, even if all possibilities of fraud are eliminated, remains questionable. the fact that the annual expenditure on allowances is ten times the amount of the support for renewable energy is a source of distortion. in the long term, therefore, emissions trading must be either fundamentally restructured or completely abolished. the environmental commitments often do not go beyond the paper on which they are written, given the billions of dollars of subsidies that are used to the contrary. it is a shame how money is redistributed and thrown out the window in this area. i cannot therefore agree with the report.
in writing. − full implementation of eu environmental legislation can create jobs and save a lot (according to studies, €72 billion per year). there are problems in the implementation of measures, in late or insufficient implementation and in 'over-implementation'. poor application is harmful to the environment and human health, causes insecurity for businesses, affects the internal market and causes additional administrative burden and costs. the aim of eu legislation is to tackle the causes of environmental damage. this concerns provisions on the legal and social responsibility of enterprises, which commit enterprises to open up to the strategy for sustainable development. the benefits include a level playing field for economic players in the internal market, the creation of incentives for innovation and the benefits for eu companies of being at the forefront. a high level of environmental protection is one of the eu's fundamental objectives and brings direct benefits to citizens, such as better living conditions through better air quality, less noise and fewer health problems.

in writing. − endocrine disruptors are chemical substances that, by virtue of their structure and mode of action, act on organisms in a way similar to hormones or affect hormone balance. the effects of endocrine disruptors have been observed in the reproduction, growth and development of certain animal species, as well as in the increase in the incidence of certain human reproductive disorders and certain cancers. this is attributed to a disorder of the endocrine system. the effects on humans are expected to include a decline in male fertility, male genital deformities, female reproductive diseases, premature puberty, and a decline in the number of boys born. similar symptoms are evident in the animal kingdom. i voted for this resolution because it is essential that further, in-depth research be carried out in the field of endocrine disruptors in order to be able to either confirm or refute the harm alleged so far.
in writing. - i am grateful for the report on the protection of public health from endocrine disruptors. finally, the dangerous consequences of excessive hormone levels are being taken seriously politically. the report unfortunately omits a major cause of the health risks that are now emerging. it has been shown that the pharmaceutical industry in particular is largely responsible for the increase in the incidence of hormone-related disorders. the problem is the pill hormone ee2, which is one of the most potent endocrine disruptors in existence. it is usually used in hormonal contraceptives. the ee2 in the ovulation inhibitors swallowed more than six million times a day completely dominates the unwanted main input into the wastewater and consequently also, unfortunately, into the groundwater and even into the drinking water. ee2 is a thousand times more potent than bisphenol a or than nonylphenol and a million times more potent than the endocrine disruptor 3-benzylidene camphor. the reach regulation is overdue for an amendment. unfortunately, it does not require a review of certain substances of concern until the annual production volume exceeds 10 tonnes. however, the production volume of ee2 is below this level, so that the worst of the worst substances falls through the reach grid. i therefore find this report critical.
in writing. − the increase in hormonal disorders and diseases in humans is to be taken very seriously. an important part of eu chemicals policy is the precautionary principle, which should not be forgotten. in particular, there is an increase in potentially reproductive diseases in the form of reduced sperm quality, testicular cancer, premature puberty and deformed genitalia. there has also been an increase in birth defects, cancers and diabetes, as well as cases of neurodevelopmental disorders such as autism and adhd. such rapid change is due to external factors. external factors include lifestyle factors, diet, pathogens, medications, exposure to chemicals, drugs, economic factors and social causes such as stress. all these factors can influence each other. the eu has an important role to play in protecting human health, and this requires the application of the precautionary principle. in everyday life, we are constantly surrounded by substances that disrupt hormones, such as packaging. young children, adolescents, and women of childbearing age are particularly at risk.

in writing. this report is about the timing of auctions of greenhouse gas emission allowances. the eu emissions trading system (eu ets) is an important tool for cost-effectively reducing industrial emissions in the eu. since the start of the eu ets, emissions have been declining and are currently marked by severe imbalances. the current economic crisis has led to an oversupply of emission allowances and a number of provisions on the transition to the third trading period (20132020). by the end of 2011, an overhang of 955 million allowances had been built up. as supply far exceeds demand, there is a significant decrease in the price of co2. therefore, this does not promote sustainable scientific and technological innovation. the report aims to clarify the timing of auctioning of allowances and, as a result, not to undermine the stability and predictability of the eu ets. short-term measures should not be seen as a solution but as an option to ensure stability until long-term structural measures are taken.
in writing. - from a purely ecological point of view, i cannot in principle agree with this proposal to suspend the eu ets for certain areas, even if only for a period of one year. however, a consensus-based, global solution is absolutely desirable, which is why the approach of compromise on the part of the european union seems to be a step in the right direction. the report is therefore unanimously approved.
i would like to thank the commissioner for his reply. i voted against the report by my colleague othmar karas because i consider it to be a mere showcase. if today the finnish prime minister katainen has been talking about the need to follow rules, then this is a rule that is certainly not being followed. there's been other rules that have been broken. i am thinking, for example, of the no-bailout clause or the maastricht criteria which were not respected and which in turn fuelled and made possible the financial crisis. this proposal contains numerous possibilities for circumventing bonuses. it is simply naive to believe that this provision will make it impossible to pay bonuses to bank managers who engage in speculation. there are many ways around it. there is no culture change in the banking sector. i would like to ask the commissioner whether he has not already made a statement on this matter. if i look at how the original article 90, which is supposed to deal with this question, has changed compared with the new article 90 which has been adopted, it is clear that the bank managers have changed their minds again. they've packed so many loopholes into this regulation that it's not worth the paper it's written on. in the end, we continue to feed banks that must be allowed to go bankrupt. the only clearing effect that would occur would be if speculators lost their speculation if you let the banks go bankrupt. it's the only thing that's really effective.
in writing. − in theory, the banking reform package with a limit on bankers' bonuses, tightened capital requirements for banks and simplified lending to smes may sound quite good. if in future the bonus payments of bankers are to be limited to an annual salary, then the willingness to put the respective credit institution in serious difficulties by engaging in high-risk speculative activities will be significantly reduced. however, experience has shown that further tightening of capital requirements will go hand in hand with a further shortage of credit for smes and will run counter to the plan of simplification for smes. i also think it is a serious systemic error if the new european banking supervision does not provide for the separation of investment banking from traditional banking. i cannot therefore agree with the report.
in writing. - the basel iii compromise is a major milestone in many ways! the crd-iv package adopted today is an important step towards banking union. from january 2014 we will gradually have more and better equity, better liquidity standards, additional, countercyclical and systemic capital buffers, better transparency rules and a compensation factor for smes and start-ups. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the banking system is able to recover from and stabilise itself in the event of a new crisis. another new feature is that for the first time there will be a bonus limit for bank managers! this is a great success for the european parliament! however, further regulation of the financial market is necessary! the fact is that business is increasingly being shifted to the unregulated world of shadow banking. we cannot allow shadow banking to be used as a backdoor for the financial industry. the commission must act very quickly and close this regulatory gap!
i would like to thank the commissioner for his reply. if you do the right thing at the wrong time, it's wrong. this proposal for the implementation of basel iii, as proposed here in the report by mr karas, comes at the wrong time. just when the economy needs the liquidity of the banks, basel iii requires a higher capital ratio for the banks. this is a bad time. this would have been a regulation that should have been made at a time when the economy was booming. now it's being arranged at the wrong time. the whole shadow banking problem is unresolved. the urgent need to reinstate the separate banking system, which was unfortunately eliminated under clinton worldwide, is not being addressed. that was a big mistake. roosevelt had that rule in place after the great depression and the bank crashes, and it turned out to be right. the distortion of competition is not being addressed by continuing to feed sick banks at the taxpayer's expense. if commissioner barnier is now proposing a regulation for june which would finally involve the shareholders, speculators, investors and investors, rather than the taxpayer, then that is the right way to go. but we have not yet had any, and unfortunately this report does not have any. that is why i voted against this report.
in writing. - to prevent a repeat of the crisis, a limitation of bankers' bonuses, which i am in favour of, will not be sufficient. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the system is not affected by the current crisis. the new european banking supervision does not provide for the separation of investment banking from traditional banking. if banks can continue to speculate on the devil's play, it is only a matter of time before credit institutions are once again on the verge of bankruptcy and have to be bailed out by taxpayers' money. until this serious system error is finally eliminated, the basic problem will remain. i therefore abstained.

in writing. − the report makes clear references to ‘banking regulations measures’ that stabilise the european banking sector and could be a solution for many of the issues that arose from the financial and economic crisis within european countries in the last few years. the overall objective is to harmonise the capital requirements of european banks and set them at the same level. the positive aspects of a ‘single banking regulation’ are: it will secure money deposits, and strengthen loans and financing methods for smes – meaning that credit availability for smes will increase, providing and ensuring an adequate credit flow and transfer to the real economy, translated into economic growth and new employment opportunities for our citizens. other positive aspects are: the leverage ratio – that could and should be looked at as a ‘safeguard’ instrument against the ‘bankruptcy risk’ and other different risks that would be associated with the ‘increase in investments’ of the institutions and companies; the capital and liquidity ‘buffers’ that would counterbalance the lending activities of the banks, reduce the probability of credit bubbles and ensure the necessary liquid means (liquidity coverage ratio) so that banks are in a position to cover losses should that be the case, in order to avoid economic and political disasters, like, for instance, greece and cyprus.
in writing. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a common position on the proposal for a directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the labelling, presentation and advertising of foodstuffs for sale to the ultimate consumer. in principle, i am in favour of this approach, since competition is important for the economy. in this case, as so often, the devil is in the detail. firstly, i think this is a matter which should be left to the member states. the subsidiarity principle is being violated here for the first time. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the airport infrastructure is not affected by the introduction of the new airport infrastructure. this would have many negative consequences for air passengers. the amendments would have particularly negative consequences for airport workers, as the new rules would lead to wage dumping. this would certainly be a false signal, one which the eu should not send, especially in difficult economic times. it can be seen that the existing arrangements ensure sufficient competition and also ensure the necessary quality and a corresponding level of pay. i therefore express my clear opposition to this report and its demands.
in writing. the european commission, in its proposal for the reorganisation of ground transport services, is pursuing the path of liberalisation at all costs. i voted against this report because this opening up of the market does not lead to more quality and better competition. on the contrary, competition is carried out on the backs of the workers. the massive price pressure will necessarily reduce quality for passengers. this is the wrong way. unfortunately, the conservative-liberal majority in the european parliament is also following a dogmatic market ideology. the text does not include any mandatory provisions on health and safety measures, nor does it take sufficient account of the principle of subsidiarity. the commission has also rejected takeover guarantees for the employees in all the ground handling sectors. the trade unions have rightly opposed this regulation and have gone on strike in front of the european parliament both in strasbourg and in brussels. i fully support the trade unions and the ground transport workers and therefore regret that mr zasada's report has been adopted.
in writing. - it is difficult to see why, after catching large quantities of fish, one should bother to throw certain species back into the sea. the fact that fish that is perfectly fine is thrown overboard is considered incomprehensible and even immoral in view of the problems of feeding the world's population. however, the report contains sound information, in particular as it aims to develop uniform rules for fishing in the skagerrak area and also reports on possible control instruments to facilitate this.
in writing. - in general, the pursuit of equal treatment is welcome. however, history has shown that the best intentions have often been used to miss the mark. the commission has also proposed that the commission should be given the task of drawing up a report on the implementation of the directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. i therefore rejected the report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i consider it very important to implement the equal treatment directive in access to and supply of goods and services. the report rightly criticises the fact that the directive has been transposed into national law only in part in an unsatisfactory or delayed manner. gender discrimination still exists, particularly in the setting of insurance premiums for life insurance or in the provision of credit. the report calls on the commission to provide comprehensive data in this context. in addition, good suggestions are made on how to close existing gaps in equality legislation.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i am a strong supporter of the principle of equal treatment between women and men and i strongly believe that ‘rights’ should be ‘equal’ for all citizens of europe without taking into consideration their gender. in my opinion, equality of women and men should be treated on a large scale of areas, like ‘gender pay gap’, unemployment, job offers, violence against women and, last but not least, in the access to and supply of goods and services field. i voted in favour of the report because, in my opinion, there is still a lot to do in order to achieve gender equality and to improve the economic (and political) situation and position of women all over the world.
in writing. - we must give the developing countries the opportunity to extricate themselves from the crisis. the traditional development aid can be considered a failure. development aid is always expensive, often ineffective and sometimes even harmful, because the specific problems of a country are often or all too often not addressed. however, the eu's trade policy in developing countries has not been as successful as it should have been, and competition with other eu policies has often exacerbated the problem. if we give money to small farmers in africa, for example, and at the same time ruin them with subsidized agricultural products, we end up throwing billions out the window. this will change little as long as we continue to support large corporations in the eu and indirectly in developing countries. i therefore do not consider this report to be useful and have rejected it.
in writing. the report also examines the role of trade and investment-led growth in developing countries. trade and investment are instruments to achieve the objectives, but cannot be the only determinants of growth and sustainable development, as structural deficits, such as in infrastructure, impede full access to world trade. competitiveness and productivity are increased, social cohesion is improved and inequality is tackled. the effectiveness is reduced by lack of coordination and can reduce citizens' confidence in the measures. full transparency must be ensured in respect of payments made by european companies to governments. a coordinated system (unctad and wto) should be established to facilitate international, national and local cooperation between donors. international investment agreements should be reformed to strengthen the development dimension.

i would like to thank the commissioner for his reply. yesterday, commissioner barnier said that he wanted to see a future in which it was not the taxpayer who had to pay for the failure of banks, but investors and speculators, shareholders and shareholders and holders of deposits of over eur 100 000 in bank accounts. and now we are demanding the exact opposite and are trying to extend the already problematic esm as an instrument for the area that is not part of the eurozone. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. if you say a yesterday and z today, that is simply the opposite of what was announced yesterday politically. i am therefore surprised that the majority groups did not take yesterday's debate to heart enough to at least slow down and send this report back in the light of the announcements made by commissioner barnier, who has indeed announced a proposal for the house for june which is the exact opposite of what has been proposed by mrs danuta hübner. i am also surprised that more colleagues have not recognised this contradiction and have not defended themselves against it.
in writing. - the creation of a financial assistance facility for member states whose currency is not the euro sounds good at first. why should there be such a construct in the form of the efsf or the esm only between the euro countries? the title alone tells us that the eu is once again ready to break the treaty without any qualms. it provides for a ban on bailout, i.e. a ban on direct or indirect state financing by the eu or any of its member countries. the second major problem is that once again a construct is being created here to draw taxpayers' money to the rescue of banks and to redirect it. that is absolutely unacceptable. the banking sector, like other sectors of the economy, needs to be restructured. not every bank is systemically relevant. the danger of further bankruptcy and waste of taxpayers' money is therefore a factor which has led me to vote against the proposal for a regulation.
in writing. - as the rapporteur herself states that she 'cannot cover all the issues [...] which are addressed in this particularly important proposal for a regulation', this interim report cannot be accepted in its present form. at least some mention of any other relevant areas would be necessary to obtain a comprehensive and consistent picture. i am generally in favour of the calls by the honourable member for sufficient transparency and accountability in the context of these instruments. the commission's proposals for the modification of the esm (in the form of an opening) and for another recapitalisation instrument in the form of a loan are also very problematic, as they involve far too great risks. they are therefore not acceptable. that is why we can only abstain.
in writing. − the ecb's annual report 2011 provides a good overview of the ecb's activities, especially in the context of the euro crisis. for a critical reader, it shows very clearly how much the ecb has extended its real mandate of ensuring price stability in the euro area independently and without any legal basis. the purchase of bonds, even on the secondary market, is not the ecb's responsibility and constitutes a covert state financing. printing money will not solve the problems in the eurozone, which is a misconception in itself. the report does not, of course, seek to criticize the work of the ecb, but rather to praise this failed policy, so i can only vote against it.
in writing. − parliament wants the ecb to be more accountable and transparent in its activity, by requesting that the eu’s central bank be more effectively involved on matters and topics with regard to economic growth and employment opportunities in the current context of the financial crisis that has conquered almost all eu member states. until now and during its mandate the ecb has followed its clearly defined role, by supporting the economic confidence of the euro area and maintaining financial market stability. the ecb has managed to avoid major economic disasters within the european union by adjusting the eu area and helping the ‘problem countries’. in order to function well, properly and normally the ecb has to preserve its independence. that is why i favour better communication and coordination between the eu institutions involved in defining and implementing monetary policy within the euro area and, at the same time, independence in the ecb’s action planning. i think that an answer to all ‘crisis questions’ could be the drafting, implementation and developing of a ‘single monetary security mechanism’, an ‘eu resolution fund’ – this would, first of all, secure citizens’ existing money deposits and reduce imbalances for competiveness.
in writing. - the value of vouchers in the eu is around 52 billion euro per year. as a result, vouchers have become a significant economic factor. the highest share, 70%, is in the telecommunications sector, followed by gift vouchers and vouchers for discounts. the different taxation of vouchers in the different countries means that multinational groups in particular are faced with the problem of offsetting and double taxation. this often creates legal uncertainty for the end-user and the consequence is that the vouchers are mostly redeemed in the home country. i voted against the report because, although the rapporteur speaks of the flexibility of the countries to ensure the proper and effective implementation of the provisions envisaged, the report does not explain what the actual implementation of the provisions should be.
in writing. - a uniform vat system for vouchers at european level is useful for several reasons: it helps to avoid tax evasion and double taxation, and thus creates legal certainty for consumers and suppliers. the directive lays down a europe-wide definition of vouchers and the time and place of their taxation. the committee on budgetary control has also adopted a number of amendments to the proposal for a directive on the taxation of savings income and capital gains. it is regrettable, however, that the report does not, in my view, take sufficient account of the rights and needs of consumers.
in writing. this report deals with a common vat system as regards the treatment of vouchers. this has a positive impact on businesses, as it eliminates double taxation and uncertainties about tax obligations. it also allows loopholes in tax evasion to be plugged. the consumer will no longer have to face a tax obstacle to using pan-european systems. harmonised rules create more clarity and consistency across the eu. as mobile devices are becoming more common (see digital agenda strategy), a distinction needs to be made between prepaid telecommunications credit (vouchers) and non-local payment services (another type of taxation). a uniform legal framework for vouchers is essential to implement the envisaged changes to the supply-side rules for business-to-consumer transactions.
in writing. − the 2007 hague convention aims to make child support available across national borders. 50 countries have agreed to a new convention under which children will receive assistance from the authorities of the participating countries in enforcing their claims. the agreement helps children to trace the debtor, to find out his financial situation and, if necessary, to obtain support by force. this is an agreement that guarantees international state support for children in the enforcement of their legitimate rights. the hague convention on child support, agreed today, provides for the establishment of central authorities which will assist children in claiming their support; it also contains rules on the procedure for the assertion of maintenance rights abroad and their enforcement. i am voting in favour of the proposal because everything must be done to help children to achieve their rights. there must be no place for a person who is liable to pay maintenance to hide behind borders.
in writing. − the content of the report is to be welcomed as the international promotion of child and other family support is an important step towards a fair and practical maintenance law and contributes to strengthening the rights of children and families. legal networking and cooperation between eu member states should be positively assessed and further promoted.

in writing. − citizens of ukraine are required to have a visa to enter the eu. on 8 april this year, ukrainian president viktor yanukovych signed a new law that facilitates the entry of eu citizens into ukraine. in return, the eu will facilitate the entry agreement with ukraine. the current visa facilitation agreement has been in force since 2008 and is now to be supplemented by further facilitations. these include the requirements for the purpose of entry documents, the provisions on the validity of multiple-entry visas, the revision of the system of the fee for urgent applications and the exemption from the visa requirement for holders of biometric service passports. i voted against the report because in the long term, visa facilitation for ukrainian citizens is likely to lead to complete visa-free travel. this could further lead to more and more ukrainian citizens entering the country not for purely tourist or professional purposes, but increasingly being used for illegal work as cheap labour.
in writing. − on 8 april 2013, ukrainian president viktor yanukovych signed a new law that facilitates the entry of eu citizens into ukraine. in return, the eu is now looking to relax the entry agreement for ukrainian citizens: the existing visa facilitation agreement is to be supplemented by further facilitations, such as the documents required to confirm the purpose of entry, the rules on the validity of multiple visas, the revision of the system of fees for urgent applications or the exemption from the visa requirement for holders of a biometric service passport. i am critical of the report and voted against it because there is a danger that liberalisation will be exploited and abused to gain a foothold in the eu as cheap black labour.
in writing. the rapporteur has dealt with the respective facilities for citizens of the union and citizens of the contracting parties. it focuses on intercultural contacts between eu and non-eu citizens, which effectively promotes the development of democracy, the rule of law and human rights. the aim is to eliminate fees and simplify requirements for the population. the protection of public security is the subject of a union safeguard measure, i.e. a possible suspension in the event of abuse, for example in the case of the asylum system. this safeguard measure constitutes a strong reservation on the part of the union, without which such an agreement would be unthinkable. in view of these advantages, the agreement should be approved, provided that it is applied in a non-abusive manner.

in writing. the hong kong convention is the first international agreement on shipwrecks. in reality, however, it still appears that most eu-flagged vessels are scrapped in countries such as india, pakistan and bangladesh. it can be said that the hong kong convention will not be fully implemented until 2020 de facto. according to this report, because of the diversity of hazardous substances on board a ship, any ship leaving the eu for scrapping is considered hazardous waste and can therefore only be legally scrapped in oecd countries. however, this provision is almost systematically circumvented. according to the eu impact assessment, over 90% of eu-flagged vessels were scrapped outside the oecd in 2009. this has serious consequences for both people and the environment in south-east asian countries. i abstained because the report clearly shows that there are still many discrepancies and contradictions between the hong kong convention and the basel convention, which i believe should be eliminated immediately. the legal situation as it stands leaves too much room for manoeuvre for ship owners which must be closed immediately.
