in writing. − partnerships and agreements between the eu and its neighbours are designed not only to win over current and future economic partners, but also to strengthen the societies of those countries and to align their policies with eu principles. the neighbourhood policy and its projects are therefore also central to european foreign policy, but they also have some shortcomings in their implementation. it is therefore essential to link these countries to europe and to strengthen relations through good neighbourliness, for example in the form of anti-corruption aid. i think it is irresponsible, however, to grant these countries visa-free travel or free movement to europe at this very moment, and to seek a neighbourhood policy in the politically unstable middle east. that is why i have refrained from making this request.
in writing. − this resolution defines the european neighbourhood policy in terms of a deepened partnership. the aim is to create an area of prosperity based on good neighbourliness, based on the union's values. the priority is security, solidarity and prosperity, which must be reciprocated. the eastern partner countries should also be supported in terms of their economic development. the major objectives of the action plan are the movement of goods, the abolition of trade restrictions, trade, international standards, cooperation in the fields of justice and home affairs, transport, science, research and development, human rights, fundamental rights and culture. the interim balance of the european neighbourhood policy was very different. in some countries, such as germany, finland and slovakia, the european neighbourhood policy has been successful. france, romania and hungary have been less successful. the content of the action plans also varied widely, and the effectiveness of the support for political institutions was also assessed very differently. the basic problem is that political support is very weak in some cases and not uniform overall. the commission's proposal is to be adopted by the council at the next meeting of the european council. the commission has already taken a number of initiatives in this area, including the establishment of a european network of national experts in the field of environmental protection.
in writing. − i welcome the european semester instrument in principle, as it has already demonstrated successes in pressing for reforms in member states. however, it must be made clear that more than 80% of the recommendations have still not been implemented and, even worse, in some areas and member states, no approaches to reform are visible. in particular, however, i would like to point out the much overdue reforms of pension, health and care systems in many member states, where the responsible governments have a huge responsibility towards the generations of today and tomorrow to create long-term financial security for these systems. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. it is therefore regrettable that the decisions and findings of the green and white papers on the future-proofing of pension systems have not been taken into account to the full. i draw from what i have said a serious warning: if the necessary reforms are not undertaken as quickly as possible, this will only benefit those populists who are harnessing the discontent of the citizens and then not only endanger prosperity and social peace but destabilise our entire democratic system.
in writing. − the european semester is designed to improve the eu's economic and monetary policy and to promote overall growth through specific strategies, as part of the europe 2020 project. this includes extending the repayment periods of so-called 'deficit countries' while supporting growth-promoting investment opportunities in so-called 'surplus countries' with sufficient fiscal space. i voted against this proposal because i believe that this report does not simply call on the member states with economic growth to inject new funds into the deficit countries, but that these investments will only lead to the strengthening of the banks.
in writing. − the european semester is an eu measure to tackle the imbalances in the competitiveness of member states that have become particularly apparent since the eu financial crisis, but which were not caused by it. they stem from the original problem of the introduction of the euro. the same monetary policy through the single currency meets very different national fiscal policies within the eu. the european semester is now issuing binding recommendations to member states to tackle these imbalances. as morally decent as this approach is, it forgets the lessons of history that centrally planned economic policies are unlikely to succeed, with or without a wall. to take just one point from the report's multitude of absurd proposals, it welcomes, for example, that more competitive countries should 'export less' if possible by boosting their domestic demand. the aim here is to punish the competitive countries. the absurd implications of this for our economic system and for economic thought since adam smith are hard to imagine. such measures will reduce the eu's competitiveness as a whole in the medium and long term, by holding back successful countries rather than learning from them. i therefore reject the report and the whole institution of the european semester.
in writing. − the ‘european semester’ is a cycle of economic and fiscal policy coordination within the eu. during the european semester the member states align their budgetary and economic policies with the objectives and rules agreed at the eu level. i voted in favour of the european semester report, because it states a clear perspective of priorities that every member state and the european union as a whole should apply, in order to provide a healthy and well-functioning economy. taking into account the current context of the financial crisis in order to try restoring europe’s economy, i think we need long-term and sound investments and growth strategies. i think there is urgent action needed in areas like: investments for smes – alternative financing resources should be found; competitiveness – the european business environment should be more competitive; tax havens, combating tax fraud – better tax policies that would actually encourage investors – sound public finances; new employment opportunities for our youth generation; education; research and innovation. my belief is that in order to end this crisis situation we need to boost europe’s competitiveness in a global economy context.
in writing. the motion for a resolution on the influx of migrants in the mediterranean is based on the events of the shipwreck off the italian island of lampedusa. the eu is trying to tackle this problem by strengthening certain organisations and institutions, such as frontex or the border guards of individual member states. however, this proposal is not to be welcomed, as it would lead to a liberalization of asylum policy and would only increase the number of those illegal immigrants. moreover, the planned opening of the labour market to asylum seekers is not a solution to the asylum problem, as this would in turn encourage an unbridled flow of people into europe and would leave the continent in a chaotic and financially unmanageable situation. i therefore voted against the motion.
in writing. - the resolution is a follow-up to the tragic events off lampedusa. many steps are mentioned which are intended to help improve the conditions for asylum flows from the coast of africa. the aim is to save many lives and improve the living conditions of survivors, and this report deserves our support.
in writing. − the national security agency (nsa) surveillance operation has shown that europe is very vulnerable in terms of data protection and that the us has not complied with the so-called tftp agreement (terrorist finance tracking program) and has instead used it purely for its own interests. however, since the eu is keen to continue both the fight against international terrorism by guaranteeing freedoms and civil rights and the cooperation between the various intelligence services as such, it reserves the right to set up a supervisory authority to monitor the flow of data between intelligence services in the context of the fight against terrorism. in my opinion, this supervisory authority must be called in at all events and any breach by the intelligence services must be severely punished. that is why i voted for this motion.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to increase the amount of the appropriations for the structural funds by eur 1 billion. the commission justifies this additional amount by the low revenue from customs duties and vat in the current year. it is significant that in addition to the supplementary budget of eur 3.9 billion, there is a hole of eur 2.7 billion in the eu coffers. the eu is obliged by the treaty to balance its balance sheet. the eu commission announced that it would be insolvent by mid-november if the €2.7 billion were not approved under the urgency procedure. a week ago, in the course of the trilogue negotiations on the eur 3.9 billion amending budget no 8, there was no talk of a bankruptcy threat. it is incredible that the commission only discovered the alleged bankruptcy over the weekend. it is a shame that the budgetary authority is informed at the last minute. if the eu cannot meet its payment obligations, it must save more, and there is plenty of saving potential. the commission's blackmailing approach is to be rejected in the strongest possible terms, and i express my rejection of the report in this way.
in writing. − draft amending budget no. 6 (dab no 6) represents a revision of forecasts of different revenues to the eu budget (vat, gni and traditional own resources (tor) – such as customs duties and different levies – e.g. sugar sector levies) and is ‘crucial to avoid cash shortages that could lead to an implementation deficit in 2013’. in order to avoid europe’s insolvency and other negative effects for the 2014 budget and the multiannual financial framework (where negotiations are still going on) for the new financial period 2014-2020, i think it is of utmost importance that the european union provides viable solutions, so that member states/beneficiaries still receive their resources. it makes no sense to stop the ‘economic engine’ at this moment, because payments that need to be made from dab 6 refer to projects already implemented, eligible from the financial period 2007-2014. in the end payments will have to be made. postponing this decisions and payments will only mean more ‘financial resources shortfalls’ next year and uncertainty in next year’s budget and financial and programming period; the eu budget is not allowed to have any debts according to the treaty.
in writing. − the european union sets out the medium-term objectives of european environmental policy for several years each by means of an environment action programme (eap). the sixth environmental action programme, which covered the period 2002 to 2012, expired at the end of july last year. the commission is now preparing a seventh environmental action programme. an important objective is to take measures to protect the environment. as a comprehensive concept, the 7th environment action programme can serve both as the european union's major environmental manifesto to its citizens and the rest of the world, and as the founding document of a european ecological new deal ahead of the 2020 horizon, as a driver of 'greener' growth and a tool for job creation. there is no question that we must not continue to exploit the environment and must also be careful to exploit the resources that we have, such as oil and gas. in addition, a minimum level of environmental technology standards should be respected in the extraction of raw materials. however, the primary responsibility should remain with the individual countries in order to prevent exploitation by large global corporations. i think it makes little sense for the eu to behave like an 'environmental police'. that is why i voted against the report.
in writing. − this resolution sets out a new general environmental action programme of the european union for the period up to 2020. the programme covers topics such as the destruction of ecosystems, energy consumption and pollution. the programme should combine an environmental message with economic and industrial concerns, and the actors should work together to develop an innovative and forward-looking approach. however, in order to achieve 'green growth', more and more complex environmental regulations are emerging, which overlap and are difficult to understand. furthermore, smes have no means of complying with the requirements. another problem is the considerable differences between member states and implementation. in addition, eu environmental legislation is not based on a solid scientific basis, and therefore has little acceptance and is difficult to enforce. i think that the environment action programme does not yet have a clear strategy. these and other clear messages should be formulated. what is the role of the citizen and how can environmental awareness be raised among the citizen? i voted against the environment action programme because of the many ambiguities and the lack of a clear strategy.
in writing. − this report aims to create a new european union environment action programme for the period up to 2020, under the theme 'living well within the limits of our planet'. the aim is to link an environmental message with economic and industrial policy concerns and to optimise the use and effectiveness of eu grants. the combination of all these factors leads to the conclusion that the present report is acceptable.
in writing. - when radiation is mentioned in the context of nuclear energy, it refers to a very specific type of radiation: ionizing radiation. it is produced by the decay of radioactive atoms, which release energy in the form of radiation, ionizing radiation. in colloquial language, ionizing radiation is often mistakenly called radioactive radiation. however, radioactivity is the property of radioactive atoms that decay and emit ionizing radiation. the dangers of ionising radiation depend on the nature, energy and duration of the radiation and the route of exposure. alpha radiation has a short range, so it is largely harmless outside the body. inside the body, however, it can damage tissue. newly collected data are now to be incorporated into legislation and natural radiation sources are also to be included in the basic standards directive. i abstained because i agree with the rapporteur that there is a danger of a reserve legislation. the rapporteur notes that the proposed provisions on environmental criteria are intended to ensure that the protection of humans is also ensured by means of rules for the protection of non-human species. however, since it is not yet possible to determine on a sound scientific basis the effects of radiation on non-human species, such regulations cannot provide better protection for humans.

in writing. the compromise between parliament and the council is the result of lengthy negotiations. in my opinion, the outcome of the negotiations is not ideal, but it is the best possible outcome that could be achieved under the current political circumstances. a compromise was necessary to ensure the political viability of the european union in the years ahead. the multiannual financial framework sets out not only the financial allocation but also the political priorities for the next seven years. the parliament and the socialist group have had a positive influence on the multiannual financial framework. for example, in the case of the increase in erasmus+ funding or the youth guarantee. the future budget should also allow for greater flexibility to respond to current policy developments. the commission has already submitted a proposal for a regulation on the application of the principle of equal treatment for men and women in matters of employment.
in writing. − the mff is a spending plan that translates the eu priorities into financial terms and is the basis for the annual budgetary exercise. it sets the maximum annual amounts the eu may spend in different political fields and therefore provides a political as well as a budgetary framework for the benefit of 500 million europeans. the european council decided in february that the new mff will be lower than the current one. the agreement reached on 11 november in brussels between parliament and the council ends the budgetary negotiation for 2014 and the next programming period, considering all negotiations and political agreements to have been decided retrospectively, bearing in mind the proposals and opinions of all the eu institutions attempting to cover all the perceived weaknesses of an economy struggling with a financial crisis. the mff includes new initiatives to help young europeans find jobs and small and medium enterprises gain access to badly needed investment funds, and it ensures that all obligations for the 2013 eu budget will be met, enabling the eu to start the financial period without the kind of unpaid claims made in the past. the mff includes an important deal on flexibility which limits the maximum possible expenditure for a european union of 28 member states to 1.0 % of the eu’s gross national income (gni) in commitments.

in writing. - youth unemployment is growing alarmingly in the member states of spain, italy and france. as this is a problem that threatens to affect the economic development of the eu and its member states, the budgetary authority, together with the commission and the european council, decided to provide additional resources under the esf (european social fund) for the above mentioned member states to combat youth unemployment. since youth unemployment, especially in the countries mentioned, requires preventive measures and the eu is using the financial resources appropriately to prevent, among other things, mass migration within europe as part of the labour market, i have agreed to this request.
in writing. − this amending budget provides for an increase of eur 150 million in appropriations for 2013. the aim of this appropriation is to combat unemployment in france, italy and spain by increasing the european social fund (esf). the european union has a long history of supporting the development of the european economy. we must therefore now invest in the fight against unemployment, especially youth unemployment, and in the fight against social exclusion.
in writing. − i voted in favour of dab no 7 as the amounts of this draft budget refer to a commitment appropriation increase in the mff, financial means mobilised in order to help people in need. these commitments will increase the european social fund (esf) allocations for three member states: france, italy and spain where the financial crisis struck, increasing the unemployment rate considerably. the esf is european union’s main instrument for supporting jobs, helping people get better jobs and ensuring fairer job opportunities for all eu citizens. it works by investing in europe’s human capital – its workers, its young people and all those seeking a job, in fact europe’s citizens.
in writing. − i voted in favour of draft amending budget no 8, as i truly believe that, generally speaking, a new financial period should not begin with unpaid bills from previous years, in this case from the last mff period. dab no 8 reflects the outstanding additional payment appropriations required to meet year-end needs across the 2013 budget. parliament and the council reached a political agreement on 11 november 2013 regarding the mff, and dab no 8 goes hand-in-hand with this agreement, which includes an important deal on flexibility which will allow maximum use to be made of funds, after the member states substantially reduced the financial amount for the mff as compared with the original commission proposal. this will, in theory, enable situations like this, where designing dab no 8 was necessary, to be avoided in the future.
in writing. − the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) was set up to provide additional support to workers suffering from the effects of the economic crisis. in recent years, spain has been particularly affected by this, for example in the construction industry, where the global financial and economic crisis has led to a sharp rise in unemployment, particularly in the spanish regions such as the comunidad valenciana. the egf is intended to provide financial resources to member states to provide vocational guidance, business support, support for business start-ups, etc. as measures to reintegrate into the world of work. i welcome this proposal because i think it is important that the eu, especially in times of crisis, sends an important signal by making meaningful investments to combat unemployment, and i therefore vote in favour of it.
in writing. − the egf is designed to provide additional support to workers who suffer from the effects of globalisation and to facilitate their reintegration into the labour market. the application from spain for the company active in the manufacture of glass and glassware, ceramics and processing of stone and earth was examined, and concerns 630 redundancies in 140 companies. the labour market in the comunidad valenciana has been severely affected by the crisis. the unemployment rate increased significantly from 9,61% in the first quarter of 2008 to 29,19% in the first quarter of 2013. the application met all the requirements and the report was therefore approved.
in writing. the government procurement agreement (gpa) is an international agreement on procurement standards for government procurement. such agreements are always a dangerous wedge between the hoped-for economic benefits and the well-being of their own people. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competition' in the definition of the term 'competition'. environmental aspects may now be taken into account in the award of contracts and the punishment of misconduct by companies by future exclusion from the award of contracts is also allowed. this should not, however, prevent the complexity of the system from increasing, particularly as the scope of the directive is extended to include other public authorities and services for ordinary citizens. in addition, the degree of foreign influence on important areas of national or regional welfare could increase. the extent to which a correct sense of responsibility or sustainability in the actions of foreign investors can be expected here remains questionable. this can also lead to the displacement of small local firms by large international firms. the dangers of this new agreement outweighing the possible benefits, i voted against it.
in writing. − the european exchange programmes, which have been successful for decades and have now been re-classified as 'erasmus+', are also an effective measure in the fight against youth unemployment. the experience gained abroad, mobility and language skills have a demonstrable and significant impact on job opportunities for young people. i am particularly pleased that the education committee of the european parliament has succeeded in pushing through an increased budget for erasmus+ in the financial framework until 2020. at eur 14.8 billion, there is significantly more money available than before. the erasmus for students, comenius for pupils, leonardo da vinci for apprentices, grundtvig for adult education and the new funding opportunities for youth and sports can thus develop their potential even more and offer a european perspective to even more learners. this is a great success for the european parliament. since 1987, erasmus+ has helped to finance some 3 million young people to study abroad. more than 45 000 austrian students have gained experience abroad. the commission has already taken a number of measures to improve the quality of the information provided by the member states. erasmus+ is much more than a traditional mobility programme. for example, for the first time, students, especially those at the master's level, will be able to take out loans for study abroad on favourable terms.
in writing. − i am very pleased that we have been able to achieve an increase in the erasmus+ budget in the context of the negotiations on the financial framework. erasmus is one of the most successful and well-known programmes of the european union. the commission has already taken a number of measures to promote the development of the european audiovisual industry. for crisis-ridden europe, with record levels of youth unemployment, investing in youth, employment, education and innovation is more important than ever. with erasmus+, we are not only giving young people the chance of a better future, but we are also paving the way for a 'european' generation that is internationally connected. it is therefore all the more important to ensure that support is equally accessible to all and not socially selective. elements such as student loans may be additional measures only and not replace scholarships.
in writing. − the eu's various mobility programmes are very popular, offering the chance to study and work in other countries. the impact on european citizens is many-sided and above all very positive (personal development of young people, foreign languages, mobility, etc.). transnational cooperation between institutions is encouraged. in times of high youth unemployment, investment in the youth sector must be given priority. for this reason, it is essential that the budget for this project be increased. the budget line for youth, as requested by the rapporteur, is also very welcome. the social partners should also be involved in the work of the programme committee.

the rapporteur. mr president, i would like to thank the commissioner for his reply. the committee on women's rights and the committee on legal affairs worked closely together after several meetings of shadow rapporteurs and with the involvement of a wide range of stakeholders. we talked to a lot of people involved. we have voted with the committees which have delivered their opinions. so we really talked to a lot of people who were affected. the report we are now presenting is well founded. it is realistic and goes beyond the commission's proposal. firstly, we need a binding regulation to ensure that we have a balanced ratio of men and women on supervisory boards, among non-executive directors. the european countries which have already introduced binding rules are particularly successful - france, for example, or the shining example of norway, which we have repeatedly cited. equality between women and men is a fundamental principle of the european union. it has been improved and refined many times since the treaty of rome and is therefore an important basis for us. we also need good european corporate governance and more diversity, gender diversity, if we are to counteract all these bouts of greed that we have seen with the financial crisis. this regulation that we lack, so this element of gender diversity can and should help to change the standard thinking patterns accordingly and to break the old boys' networks. now for the substance: we want to increase the proportion of the underrepresented sex to 40% by 2020. that is what the commission proposal says. we want to do this through a sort of procedural quota, by shedding more light on the issues, by using transparent selection procedures and by applying qualification criteria from the outset. so now, when headhunting firms are employed or commissioned, this principle should be a thread running through the whole process. i mentioned it before: it is about breaking down the old boys' networks, where more or less men who have the same suit tastes, the same socio-cultural background, some of the same corporate ideas, ultimately dominate the action on the supervisory board. that's not good for business. so the point of these procedures is that they are good for women, but they are also good for men - if we apply these objective criteria - so they are good for the quality of the supervisory boards and therefore they are good for companies! the commission's proposal is now being exceeded in its scope. the commission proposal provides that all listed companies should apply the same rules, with the exception of small and medium-sized enterprises and those with a share of less than 10%, where the under-represented sex is concerned, i.e. de facto women. we're going beyond that. small and medium-sized enterprises are still excluded. i regret this personally, because these are enterprises which can be quite large - 250 employees, for example. but that is not politically feasible at the moment. that means we'll leave it at that. we are not going to allow any exceptions. and that's good, because it expands the scope. it is not just a question of whether women can carry cement bags, for example, but whether they can do a good job on supervisory boards, read financial statements, do their job. accordingly, we need not take account of the 10% clause for the criterion of its not being justified in substance. a word about the family businesses. i am very sympathetic to family businesses, but there is no useful definition at european level, not even in the national states. it is therefore not justified to exclude them from the scope of the regulation, especially when one considers that the biggest companies - i am thinking of lego, for example, or many other large companies - are excluded and that the whole scheme cannot be particularly effective in itself. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament on the subject of the financial perspective. the penalties shall be effective, proportionate and dissuasive. and so, of course, the member states are cordially invited to go beyond that. there are no limits to the imagination. we have a provision for excluding public procurement and for excluding access to the structural funds. in short, we have remained realistic. we have tried not to reach for the stars - i would very much like to do that - by taking on the boards, for example. but we can do that in a next step. it is now time to appeal to the council in particular - which is unfortunately not here, as i see it - to take this matter much more seriously!

vice-president of the commission. − mr president, permit me just to give a short answer to a specific question because, in general, i do agree with the vast majority of the speakers in this house. one question was asked about what we are doing regarding quotas and equal representation in our administrations. i can only speak here for the administration which is mine, for the european commission. one third of the commissioners, 33 %, are female, which is the best gender balance ever in the commission. we do have quotas in our administration. we have 33 % for middle management and 25 % for top management. the targets had already been met by 2012, so now we are setting the quotas higher. you have to ask the other institutions the same question and you also have to ask your governments and your national parliaments the same question. coming to the conclusions of this debate, we have seen that, despite a few voluntary initiatives at national and european level, the situation has not changed significantly in recent years. tangible progress is the exception, not the rule, and progress only becomes really strongly visible in countries which have had quota laws for some time. and who has to bear the burden? our society and our economies – because gender equality at work is not only a women’s issue: it is a business issue. it is an economic imperative. in these times of economic difficulty when we face the joint challenges of an ageing population, of falling birth rates, of skills shortages, it is more important than ever to ensure that we capitalise on the richness of human talent and skills irrespective of gender. at the heart of the proposal lies a transparent selection process aiming to reach a 40 % representation of the under-represented sex by 2020 based on clear criteria and the candidates’ skills and qualifications. the reasoning is simple. no woman will get a job simply because she is a woman. however, no woman will be denied a job any more simply because she is a woman, as is happening today. this should be a fair deal both for the business world and for women, who have the same right to pursue careers as men. so in your vote tomorrow, dear members, you have this possibility. let us stop the waste of talent and the waste of resources. let us stop denying equal chances to equally-qualified women, and let us finally crack the glass ceiling.

in writing. − i voted in favor of this report as the funds mobilised will reach our people in need, our european citizens. the use of these funds could be seen as an aid measure for europe’s inhabitants. generally, the european union financing instruments – the european social fund (esf) and the flexibility instruments – are financing instruments that help to balance and amend more efficiently ceilings under the initial financial planning of the european union, for events that could not be foreseen. the esf is europe’s main instrument for supporting jobs, helping people get better jobs and ensuring fairer job opportunities for all eu citizens. it works by investing in europe’s human capital. the flexibility instrument provides funding in a given financial year for clearly identified expenses which could not be covered by one or more budget headings without exceeding their expenditure ceilings.
in writing. − ensure the eu's competitiveness in the global satellite navigation sector. the share of european industry in the world market is small. the basis for this market is provided mainly by simple position and time signals. some 75% of the market shares are in telecommunications services, 20% in intelligent road transport systems and 5% in other applications. in addition, egnos and galileo applications contribute to the creation of quality jobs, growth and the knowledge society, and make the eu independent of us or chinese systems in the long term. if the member states do not act, the market could be taken over by third parties, which would lead to economic problems: an estimated 6% of european gdp depends on gnss applications! a european gnss can be a positive instrument to support external and internal policies. the report has my vote, because it is questionable whether the eu can afford not to participate in this new market. research and innovation are being taken to a new level here. the benefits to citizens are increasing, but so too is the risk of permanent surveillance at eu level.

in writing. − the european social fund (esf) is the european union's main financial instrument to support employment measures in the member states and to promote economic and social cohesion. the esf's expenditure amounts to around 10% of the eu's total budget. the esf is one of the eu's structural funds, which are used to improve social cohesion and economic development in the regions of the union. it is clear that it is essential to take measures to strengthen the labour markets of the individual member states to the extent that they are able to reduce unemployment significantly. nevertheless, i believe that simplified access to the esf could risk misuse of the fund. in my view, even if the rules and procedures are simplified, it must still be possible to ensure that any abuse can be excluded. i have voted against this report because it does not make this clear.

in writing. − packaged retail investment products (prips) are at the core of the retail investment market. they are products that contain an element of packaging or wrapping to an underlying investment opportunity, including shares, bonds, and other assets. statistics mention that prips make up a market in europe worth up to eur 10 trillion. these are the investment products retail investors would typically be offered by their bank when they want to make an investment, for example to save for retirement or some other target like buying a house or paying for their children’s education. i voted in favour of the amended commission proposal, as i believe that european citizens and consumers should rebuild their trust in the financial markets and at the same time they should be protected when buying financial products (for example insurance products). another important element is the key investor information document (kiid). the kiid should provide the retail investor with an adequate base for making his investment decision. however, before the final investment decision is taken, the investor may need to read the detailed and comprehensive information contained in the prospectus and contractual basis. therefore, it must be possible to have references in the kiid. in the end, the rapporteur asked for a negotiating mandate for a trialogue.

in writing. the 'circus' between the european parliament's working places in brussels and strasbourg must be brought to an end. the european parliament should have only one seat in future, in strasbourg, for several reasons. the european parliament has a duty to protect the citizens of europe. since 1952, european parliamentary assemblies have met in strasbourg, and since 1999 it has been the official and sole seat of the european parliament. that is why, some 15 years ago, a modern parliament building was built at a cost of some 450 million euros. the attempts of the opponents of strasbourg to sell a move to brussels under the guise of a 'single-seat campaign' are therefore a gross electoral deception and a waste of money, since the building in strasbourg is not to be used for anything else. moreover, the alsatian capital, which was for centuries a subject of dispute between germany and france, is a symbol not only of franco-german reconciliation after the second world war but also of peace in europe. all of this must be taken into account, which is why this false paper was rejected.
in writing. − the european parliament's monthly commuting between brussels and strasbourg is economically unjustifiable and must be stopped. however, the right to decide on the location of the parliament is currently reserved to all eu member states by unanimity. however, unlike many of my colleagues, i do not think that brussels is the most appropriate place for the ep to be. this city is badly run, unhealthy and unmanaged. concentrating all the european institutions in one city - brussels - is a very short-sighted policy. the high level of support for the ep's brussels residence is largely due to the fact that many meps have acquired property in the city. strasbourg, which has been at the crossroads of german and french history for many centuries, is a symbol of the reunification of europe. i think it is a very good place to host the european parliament. it was not without reason that in 1949 the nations of europe decided to establish the first international organization, the council of europe, in strasbourg, to promote peace on a war-torn continent. with improved infrastructure, particularly in the area of air transport, strasbourg, which already hosts the ep's main official seat, could become the sole home of the ep. but it would be even better to choose one of the capitals of the new member states as the seat of the european parliament - they still have too few european institutions, but they are a good addition to the city and national income. the latvian capital, riga, for example, could be a great home for the european parliament. the eu's functions and structure are fundamentally different from those of a state, and so its institutions need not be concentrated in a single city. by disrupting the eu institutions, citizens and employees alike will benefit.

in writing. - the new motto for supporting research and small businesses is: more money, less bureaucracy. the eu is thus providing more than ever before. the support programmes will enable smes in particular to boost research, innovation and competitiveness even more in the future. the horizon 2020 programme is designed to support research and innovation within the eu with some €70 billion. this means that in future european scientists will receive between 70 and 100 per cent of their direct costs and that funding applications will be processed more quickly. another new feature is the 'sme instrument' within research funding, which is specifically tailored to the needs of small and medium-sized enterprises in the research sector. in future, there will also be calls for tenders directed only to smes. the cosme programme is designed to boost the competitiveness of smes with some eur 2 billion. in addition to financial support, policy measures such as reducing red tape and facilitating access to finance are also to be promoted. at the same time, there are special grants for women, migrants, internationalisation measures and business start-ups. we will also develop the 'erasmus for young entrepreneurs' exchange programme under cosme.

i would like to thank the commissioner for his reply. we austrians are not a nation of deep-sea fishermen, but the ecological situation of the world's oceans is something that concerns us. so let me make a few comments. deep-sea trawl fishing is known to destroy sensitive habitats and the species that live there. however, a recent report published by the european commission highlights the potential for deep-sea species to be fished using alternative fishing methods. these cause little damage to deep-sea ecosystems. the damage caused by bottom trawling is disproportionate to the yield. in the north-east atlantic, only about 0.75% of european fisheries are harvested in this way. in addition, trawl fishing is one of the fishing methods which provides the least number of jobs in relation to the quantity of fish caught. alternative methods such as longline fishing create six times as many jobs. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's fishing fleet is not subject to any unfair competition.

member of the commission. − mr president, i wish to thank the rapporteur, marian harkin, for the constructive approach to this proposal. following fruitful negotiations between the three institutions, i believe that we have reached a common objective with the adoption of this proposal. convincing some of the reluctant member states has not been easy, and i wish to express the commission’s deep appreciation for the constant support of the european parliament throughout the negotiation process. the legislative proposal is very timely, coming as it does while a majority of our member states continue to experience the repercussions of the global financial and economic crisis. in addition, besides all the positive things that globalisation brings, we shall inevitably continue to also address the periodic adjustments it entails when it forces companies to close or relocate. the new design of the egf, i believe, will serve the purpose of providing relief and support to the affected workers. we now have a fund which has a wider scope – it can be called upon in cases of both globalisation and the crisis. the fund has a larger group of potential beneficiaries, in that self-employed, temporary and part-time workers have been added to the redundant workers who can currently be taken care of. even if not explicitly, farmers are also included among the potential beneficiaries in their capacity as self-employed. the agreed co-funding rate – although not our preferred option – now set at 60 %, is still more beneficial for all member states than the current one. last but not least, under special conditions, young unemployed can also be supported to find their place in the labour market. this is a provision which adds to the other options that member states will have in the very near future to combat youth unemployment in the most affected regions.
the commission is therefore proposing to amend the proposal. the commission is not prepared to accept this. the egf was originally an instrument that made it possible to support workers who had lost their jobs as a result of globalisation, to give them a real boost, as i say. the economic crisis came and the fund had to be extended to those workers who lost their jobs directly or as a result of the global financial and economic crisis. it was certainly a much-needed help to those affected. the present proposal is certainly outside the eu budget and, in principle, illusory in my view. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full. i have to say that the egf will now have a much smaller budget, namely eur 150 million per year, which represents a total volume of eur 1 billion for the payment period 2014-2020.

the rapporteur. - madam president, i have to say that i am very sorry. this report is about women with disabilities. as you can all imagine, women with disabilities very often experience multiple discrimination. there are 80 million people in the european union who are disabled, 46 million of them women and girls. this represents 16% of the total female population in europe. i am very sorry that we did not have a short debate or a short presentation and i hope that the report will be voted on positively.
in writing. − pericles 2020 is an exchange, support and training action programme to protect the euro against counterfeiting both in europe and worldwide. the pericles programme promotes cooperation between national, european and international authorities involved in the fight against euro counterfeiting. the support measures shall include information exchange measures (seminars, workshops, meetings and conferences), traineeships, personnel exchanges and technical, scientific and operational support measures. some €500 million of damage has been caused by counterfeiters since the introduction of the euro in 2002, despite the euro being one of the rarest of counterfeit currencies. the pericles programme has made a major contribution to this. i voted for the report because we must not give counterfeiters the opportunity to succeed in criminal activities. the significant increase in penalties has certainly done its part, but the eu must nevertheless continue to intensify its close cooperation with non-eu countries in the area of counterfeiting.
in writing. - counterfeiting is always a problem with currencies, but fortunately it is still limited in the case of the euro. this is due in particular to the fact that the design is quite secure and the control structures are defined at national level with cooperation at union level. however, the co-financing rates for the control programme are currently too high. this puts a significant cost burden on the eu funds allocated to this purpose. it is therefore proposed to reduce these funding rates and to make member states more financially responsible for protecting their currency (reduced from 80% to 70% by the eu fund). since states have a valid self-interest in keeping their currency safe, this proposal seems reasonable. i therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. − counterfeiting has a negative impact on the european economy and the stability of the currency itself. pericles makes an important contribution to effectively combating counterfeiting, for example by maximising the use of the funds provided. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect.
in writing. the report presented here is an opinion on the european statistical programme. the importance of statistics is underlined, and the rapporteur points out that accurate and professionally produced statistics are of unprecedented importance as they influence political events and policy decisions. it is also noted that the available financial resources must be allocated in a very cost-effective manner. the commission's proposal is to set up a european network of national experts to assess the impact of the eu's policies on the environment. the report can therefore be regarded as positive.
in writing. − the international labour organisation convention on decent work for domestic workers is an important step towards guaranteeing basic principles of domestic workers' rights and respect for their human and legal rights. i think it is crucial that the european parliament should make its position clear on this!
in writing. the international labour organisation convention deals with the rights and decent working conditions of domestic workers. their appreciation is the main objective of the convention. it clearly states that they are an important part of the economy, that their work has been legally undervalued in the past, and it provides a clear definition of these activities. they should be granted basic labour rights such as freedom of association, the right to collective bargaining, the right to join a trade union, the abolition of all forms of compulsory labour or child labour, the right to privacy, the right to education for those under 18 years of age, etc. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. i therefore naturally voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − domestic workers are among the least protected occupations in the world. the problems range from illegal work, exploitative working conditions, to child labour and violence. the main victims are mostly women, especially migrant women. ilo convention 189 is an important cornerstone for improving the working conditions of domestic workers. it obliges ilo member states to guarantee basic labour rights for domestic workers. the commission will also be taking targeted action against violence and child labour. i therefore naturally voted in favour of mrs zuber's report. human and workers' rights must be equally applied to all.
in writing. - domestic workers are one of the least protected but also least visible occupational groups. the special protection needs of these workers, who are often women with a migrant background or children, require increased public attention. the international labour organisation's convention on decent work for domestic workers, which was preceded by a wide-ranging global debate, is a major step towards fair treatment of this group of people. many countries, especially countries of origin, have already signed the convention. with today's vote, the european parliament has paved the way for ratification by the member states. it is important to sign this convention as soon as possible in order to combat child labour effectively and to protect domestic workers as a whole.
in writing. - the rapporteur's recommendation is aimed at the very weakest members of society, and the protection of domestic workers is a key issue. since people with a migrant background are very often affected, it is particularly important to provide comprehensible and appropriate information. the report also aims to combat human trafficking and the abuse of domestic workers and should therefore be welcomed and supported.

in writing. −development aid is always expensive, often ineffective and sometimes even harmful, because the specific problems of a country are often, or all too often, not addressed. there is a lack of sustainability and coordination of activities. in development cooperation, budgeted resources too often fail to reach the local institutions for which they are intended, or only partially. this is partly due to weak institutions in the recipient countries, but also to incorrect incentive structures and lack of accountability. it is doubtful whether an eu-wide development finance instrument will change this, especially if the eu's voting is not coherent. so when we give money to small farmers in africa, but at the same time ruin them with subsidized agricultural products, we end up throwing billions out the window. it is also important that development funding be made conditional on cooperation on refugee issues, for example through return agreements. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial instruments are used effectively. i voted against it in that sense.
in writing. - i am glad that the egf will continue in the new eu budget period! however, the decision by the member states to reduce the egf's budget from eur 500 million per year to eur 150 million per year is 'double-talking'. there's nothing left but a drop on the hot rock. the commission has also proposed that the member states should be able to take part in the negotiations on the new framework programme. we need the right structures for sustainable employability and active labour market policies. there is nothing like the dual education system in austria. the eu globalisation fund has already provided a total of eur 27 million to austrian workers. this makes austria the country that has received the highest per capita allocations from the eu globalisation adjustment fund to date. the unemployed in the federal states of lower austria, upper austria and styria in particular have benefited massively from the egf.
in writing. the egf is endowed with eur 500 million annually and is designed to help workers affected by the consequences of major structural changes in world trade patterns. it is estimated that between 35 000 and 50 000 workers could benefit from this every year. the money will be used to support measures to help people find work, individual training, self-employment and business creation, mobility grants and aid for disadvantaged or older workers. the report shows that 95 percent of humanitarian aid funds are spent on disaster response and follow-up. i believe that it is the fastest way of providing targeted aid to the affected regions and to the victims. since the report does not specify what the aid for disaster prevention should be, i am convinced that the 5% that has been allocated so far is sufficient. i have abstained because, as the rapporteur has said, i too believe that the fund is often too late. i do not think it is right to ask the member states to introduce more cost-effective measures first, which may then be uneconomical, because of a lack of money.
in writing. - i voted for the report on the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) because it has been one of the eu's most important instruments, especially in recent years, to deal with the consequences of the economic crisis. it is important that the scope of the fund has been extended to include temporary workers, temporary workers and self-employed workers, who can receive funds when they need them. the possibility of support for young people who are neither in employment nor in education or training (neets) is particularly important. i am firmly convinced that it is essential to continue the fund and secure the funding. however, given the rapid rise in unemployment in the eu, especially among young people, the fund's resources would need to be significantly increased. i believe that today's vote has sent a clear signal to the council and the member states that the fight against (youth) unemployment is a top priority for the european parliament.
in writing. − as a result of the economic and financial crisis, many european companies were forced to reduce their workforce, resulting in a dramatic increase in unemployment across europe. in 2009, the number of unemployed persons in latvia increased by 2.3 times compared to the previous year. although statistics show that the unemployment rate in latvia has decreased slightly since 2009, both due to the improvement of the economic situation and the increase in emigration, it is still above the 10% threshold, and among young people even above 19%. the european union now urgently needs to boost employment growth to restore economic growth. the european globalisation adjustment fund is an important support mechanism to help people who have lost their jobs to acquire new skills to help them re-enter the labour market, and i therefore voted in favour of continuing the fund for the next programming period 2014-2020. it should be noted that unemployment is a problem faced by people in different employment sectors, both private and public. it is important for latvia that the funds of the fund will be available not only to employees but also to self-employed persons who at a given moment do not have an income. unlike in the previous programming period, the egf will be able to be used to support young people in regions affected by unemployment. the fund is an important instrument to help the economy adapt to changing global trade conditions.
in writing. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council should be consulted on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work. the rapporteur is concerned about the more efficient use of egf funds and also talks about the co-financing, which is to be increased from 50% to 65% and in particularly affected countries to 75%. the only negative point the rapporteur mentions is the insufficient funding in the agricultural sector, which amounts to eur 2.5 billion. although this is a negative factor, the report is positive in that it aims to reduce unemployment and to reintegrate workers into working life, and it is financially supported.
in writing. the proposal for an obligation to exchange information automatically in the field of taxation is a step forward in cooperation between member states of the european union. the aim is to prevent tax evasion as much as possible and to provide financial relief to eu citizens, who otherwise compensate for the outstanding/missing money by raising taxes. it is therefore in the public interest to support this step towards eliminating tax evasion. however, particular attention should be paid to data protection, as privacy protection must be safeguarded in all circumstances and comply with the applicable eu legislation.
in writing. − the transport of radioactive material is a high-risk activity for man and the environment. there are laws to protect all those who have to deal with the materials, and they must be respected. these apply to all european internal transport. in order to comply with the directives for carriers of radioactive materials at european level, each member state has developed its own systems optimized for it. however, as these are high-risk dangerous goods, it makes sense to introduce a uniform system to be followed by each eu country. the mere fact that it is based on existing legislation such as the transport sector of the tfeu, radiation protection, the provisions for the protection of the health of workers and the general public and the euratom treaty makes uniformity necessary. that is why i voted for the report.
in writing. − radioactive waste is a serious danger and environmental burden for our children and grandchildren. careful handling is of the utmost importance. profitability and thrift are not appropriate here. to prevent this, member states have developed a number of national solutions for the registration and transport of radioactive material, including nuclear waste. the problem is that the marked differences have made transport operations even more complex and thus, in fact, more opaque at european level. the proposal now provides for a common procedure at european level. this is to ensure that administrative burden is reduced, bureaucratic costs are reduced and the safety standard is further improved. i have voted in favour of the proposal because we all want a community solution.
in writing. − in principle, the rapporteur's approach to cost-effectiveness and simplification of the registration system is to be welcomed, but the transport and storage of radioactive materials always involves considerable risks to health. nor is there any distinction made between the transport of radioactive material for medical purposes and the transport of radioactive material for the production of nuclear energy. public safety must not be compromised under any circumstances. although simplification of the registration system may at first sight appear to be the most economical solution, the risks are immeasurable.

in writing. the relatively high population density in the eu 117 people per square kilometre means that large parts of the land available to us are intensively used. this is accompanied by pressure on the remaining natural areas and the risk of their fragmentation. i am therefore pleased that the european parliament is speaking out across the political groups in favour of further developing green infrastructure in the eu. where it makes environmental and economic sense, the concept of green infrastructure needs to be implemented more systematically. clean air, clean water, flood protection green infrastructure can often deliver more cost-effective and sustainable environmental, economic and social benefits than conventional solutions. this makes it all the more important to attract private sector investment in green infrastructure projects and to facilitate access to finance.

the rapporteur. the commission has already done so. in times of economic crisis, high unemployment, high energy prices, scarcity of raw materials and dependence on imports, the creation of sustainable jobs and economic growth is essential for social cohesion. innovation is a key element in achieving this objective and should therefore be promoted. the eco-innovation approach, which combines environmental protection with growth, competitiveness and job creation, offers a way to do this. environmentally friendly innovation is fundamental to reducing greenhouse gas emissions, using resources such as water and raw materials more efficiently, increasing the use of recycled materials and producing higher quality products with lower environmental impact, to name a few. such innovations are also very important for the development of more environmentally friendly production methods. the manifestations of eco-innovation are many. the current focus areas of the eco-innovation 2012 call are: recycling of materials, sustainable construction products, food and beverage industry, water management and green enterprises. future calls for proposals should consider extending to all sectors and business activities, as eco-innovation is a cross-cutting policy area and all sectors and business activities should be eligible for support. the commission is currently promoting eco-innovation through demonstration and market-launch projects, market-based financial instruments and public-private partnerships under the competitiveness and innovation framework programme (cip). these instruments have also been included in the proposals of the horizon 2020 framework programme to ensure continuity between the cip and horizon 2020 programmes. the growth of the green technology sector - also known as green-tech or clean-tech industries - in recent years has shown that investing in green growth offers a huge opportunity for the economy. while almost every other sector of the economy has suffered significant losses as a result of the recession, the environmentally friendly economy is still expanding despite some slowdown in growth. the european organic sector generates an estimated annual turnover of eur 319 billion which is equivalent to approximately 2.5% of eu gdp and currently employs 3.4 million people. this potential is far from being exploited. these are complex challenges, including food security, climate change, soil quality, raw material scarcity, the transition to renewable energy systems, energy efficiency and more. such a transition requires a holistic approach, covering education and training, higher education, research and development, private and public investment and infrastructure development. a new, sustainable eu economy must ensure balanced economic and social development that benefits all markets and business models. it can give new impetus to traditional industries and existing jobs by adapting to sustainable, resource-efficient production and working methods. this requires the creation of new tools and the simplification of procedures so that they can also be used by smes. the inclusion of eco-innovation in the member states' strategy papers for the period 2014-2020 as a tool for building and expanding an environmentally friendly economy could strengthen cooperation between education, business and science. our report 'eco-innovation - jobs and growth through environmental policy' addresses the challenges and opportunities of the transition to a more resource-efficient and lower-carbon economy. it identifies solutions and possible solutions and focuses on the framework conditions that need to be created at european level, but also at member state level, in order to exploit the growth potential of eco-innovation to the full.
