in writing. − this directive is welcome as it aims to give all citizens access to a payment account. the commission also proposes to make banks more transparent about account fees. the directive is to be implemented in the member states as soon as possible, so that bank customers enjoy more rights and can more easily switch accounts. all people should have access to a payment account with basic features, regardless of their financial situation, employment or residence in the european union.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report because it gives a clear and transparent overview of the ‘payment accountsʼ that european citizens are able to use throughout the eu. by voting in favour of this report we vote for direct access to a basic payment bank account for everyone residing legally in one of the eu member states. secondly we voted for the ‘right to informationʼ, meaning that all bank customers should and will be informed clearly by their banks about all fees and interest rates charged. this is a simplified way of using banking sector services which should also be to the advantage of the financial services industry, because they will benefit from increased mobility and number of customers. the final vote on this report was postponed.
in writing. − the report is welcome, as maritime spatial planning and integrated coastal zone management are a topic of relevance to all member states. it is important to keep sustainable development in mind in this area and to support blue growth in the maritime sector in the long term.
in writing. − the request for a transitional period for mayotte in respect of the new eu legislation is in any case to be accepted. in any event, the island should be given sufficient time to adapt to the existing eu rules. a hasty implementation would do no one any good.
in writing. the rapporteur deals with the essential points of fisheries policy. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'commercial fishing' to cover the whole of the eu, with the exception of certain member states. the report is generally agreed as a european maritime and fisheries fund is needed, but the precise provisions on sustainability should be reviewed and revised if necessary. the final vote has been postponed.
in writing. − the 'european capitals of culture' initiative makes a significant contribution to promoting the identity of citizens as europeans and also promotes the formation of an international identity. cultural cooperation across borders is encouraged and the added value of the initiative is visible at all levels. in addition, the 'european capitals of culture' initiative has proved to be a great success in recent years and should be continued in any case. the changes envisaged in the report are positive developments. the commission is also proposing to extend the european capital of culture initiative to include the following cities:
in writing. − for the mayotte territory, and in any case for the ecosystems and wildlife therein, the change in status from 'overseas territory' to 'outermost region' has some positive consequences. various fisheries and animal health regulations will now also be valid for this area, a process which i support.
in writing. − it is necessary to examine each application by a developing country applying for special treatment under the gsp+ not only in depth but also individually. the consolidation of several applications in a single act constitutes a significant disadvantage for all applicant countries, since a single non-approval would have to reject the entire application for all countries.
in writing. - better education is widely seen as a key to better roma inclusion. in reality, however, the school situation of roma children is often more problematic than that of other pupils with a migrant background, despite the fact that there are hardly any language barriers. in many cases, it is the traditions of these groups that are hindering the improvement of living conditions. in typical good-manner, attempts have been made over the years to socialize them, and they all fail because they are not accepted by the majority of this nomadic people. this has led to the consolidation of behaviours which are seen as opposed to the cultural identity of the dominant groups' culture. the eu still has no patent recipe for the unresolved issues of establishment and possession of personnel documents, etc. the present strategy only continues this aberration. it also fails to take account of the financial burden on local authorities which arises from the free movement of persons. that is why i voted against it.
in writing. − the national roma integration strategies addressed and examined by mr aguilar represent the first positive steps towards efforts on roma integration. the rapporteur highlights the betterment of the general roma situation that has been achieved but he also stresses that there is still much room for improvement. issues that need to be addressed are the following: access to education, housing, healthcare, prevention of discrimination on ethnic grounds and the effective spending of eu funding earmarked for roma. the motion for a resolution sets out a picture of the current status of national roma integration strategies.
in writing. − the events in ukraine demonstrate the willingness of the various national societies to integrate into the european union. in the russian customs union, however, countries are being lured by blackmail, secret deals, and false promises. this action must be countered by our opposition. the european union must stand firm on its values and lend a helping hand at this historic juncture. 65% of ukrainians support closer cooperation with the eu and feel that the government is taking them into account. the people who walked through the streets did not think that the association agreement with the eu would change their lives overnight, they are ready to work hard to build a strong, orderly, rule-based ukraine that is in line with european democratic norms. all they ask is that they not be disturbed by corruption, theft of state property, secret dealings. ukrainian politicians, media and society need to know what the eu will do next if the association and free trade agreements are signed. the european commission must therefore develop concrete steps to speed up the implementation of the agreements. a new eu strategy for relations with ukraine and an emergency plan are needed. the previously proposed 600 million is not enough, considering the economic sanctions against russia. our response to russian policy must be appropriate. we must do everything possible to fulfil the aspirations of the ukrainian people!
in writing. − to create functioning and politically well-legitimated agreements, the full agreement of both parties is essential. the situation in ukraine, which is highlighted in this resolution, is a good example of this. the negotiations with azerbaijan have shown that inadequate or hesitant policies can also put potential partner countries in difficult situations. the geopolitical and economic considerations must be taken into account in a very profound way.
in writing. - the recognition of kosovo is a kind of dress rehearsal for serbia. some even want to make the european union the protector of the kosovo albanians, without taking into account the legitimate interests of the serbs. the declaration of independence by the kosovo albanians is, as is well known, clearly contrary to international law. it is in violation of un resolution 1244. it is apparently part of eu policy to legitimize this breach of international law, although some eu countries do not recognise kosovo's independence for good reasons. brussels has repeatedly stressed that it does not interfere in internal affairs. but then the recognition of kosovo must not be dictated to the serbs. i agree with the points made in the resolution concerning the continuing problems of corruption and the like. the peace process in the balkans, that is, on the doorstep of the eu, is much more important than the missions in distant countries. i have voted in favour of the resolution on these grounds.
in writing. - the rapporteur highlights the positive steps albania has taken on its aspirational path towards europe, but he also remains critical, highlighting the weaknesses in its efforts and areas where there is still room for improvement. although albania's efforts are very welcome and should not be undermined, it should be considered whether the immediate granting of candidate status would not be too hasty, especially since the violations of human rights and the discrimination against individual minorities are very serious and have a negative impact because they are not compatible with european directives.
in writing. - this package of motions for resolutions contains many different aspects, as the authors express some opposing views. it is also important to note that some of the issues raised in the motions for resolutions are highly controversial and complex. we have not yet overcome the financial and economic crisis and we still need to find more appropriate measures to help us get out of the debt crisis. as a member of the alde group, i am of the view that humanitarian and civilian foreign policy objectives should be pursued. this is how the union should present itself, above all at international level.
in writing. - the differentiated integration which is being sought is in itself very welcome; however, you must be careful not to set yourself greater goals than are realistically attainable. the present report is in principle to be regarded as positive.
in writing. − in any event, closer cooperation between the eu institutions is to be encouraged. the sooner the institutions communicate with each other, the more productive all those involved can be in their work for the citizens of the eu. small and large problems and obstacles are thus addressed at the earliest possible stage. cooperation within the eu institutions and transparent communication with citizens should be encouraged.
in writing. − it is the responsibility of man to take care of his environment and ecosystems so that they can be passed on to succeeding generations in a functioning way. in the area of infrastructure in particular, care must be taken to ensure that projects are compatible with ecosystems and do not threaten or even destroy them. this could lead to irreparable damage in the long term, which could also have a massive impact on humans. i also believe that sustainable infrastructure and its long-term planning will be necessary to maintain the quality of life of people, especially in the urban centres. however, it is to be feared that the present proposal is once again about meeting quotas from various international agreements without taking account of national circumstances. that is why i abstained.
in writing. the resolution on green infrastructure is very welcome, as unfortunately far too little attention is still paid to environmental protection and the preservation of our habitat. the natural capital of the european union must be protected, preserved and developed under all circumstances, and the measures mentioned in the field of political and economic work as well as in terms of public awareness must not be neglected. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
in writing. - the new stress tests on banks are not designed to restore public confidence. after all, many banks that had scored well in the last test soon afterward ran into trouble. similarly, the acquisition of portfolios of euro-member states' government bonds would only cause immense economic and legal problems. to prevent a new financial crisis, systemic failures such as the mixing of investment banking and traditional banking must be eliminated. if banks continue to speculate unhindered, it is only a matter of time before credit institutions are once again on the verge of bankruptcy and have to be bailed out with taxpayers' money.
in writing. − the report is very positive in its open criticism of the economic situation and its clear statement that the monetary policy transmission mechanism i.e. the effectiveness of the ecb's monetary policy on the real commodity market is no longer functioning. the report then foolishly focuses on making recommendations on how monetary policy could be better managed. it can't control anything if the transmission mechanism isn't working at the moment and monetary policy remains ineffective on the rest of the economy. the report also has some schizophrenic features. the omt programme for the purchase of government bonds is praised on the one hand, but condemned on the other. the ecb's monetary policy is also lax, and concerns are expressed about inflation, while it is also mentioned that medium-term inflation expectations encourage the ecb to continue to pump money into the money supply. the report is a symbol of the fact that the fronts are not along the political groups but along the national borders. representatives of the southern countries are in favour of continuing the ecb's policy, while representatives of the 'fiscal north' of europe, including austria, are against the ecb's continued inflationary policy, especially as it has no effect on the real economy anyway, but greatly increases the risk of inflation. i could not agree to such a chaotic report without a half-clear position.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the european central bank (ecb) annual report for 2012 as it gives a very clear overview of the ecbʼs work in 2012 and the steps still to be followed up during 2013. in my opinion, the economic situation of europe generally, and that of european banking systems in particular, is still fragile and needs efficient and responsible monitoring and supervision. even though ecb measures and action taken last year as an emergency method to deal with the effects of the financial crisis and to stabilise the euro area had positive results, we should bear in mind that the policy measures were ‘intended to be transitoryʼ. the instruments used to stimulate economic growth and improve the labour market situation ‘revealed their limitsʼ and we should be aware that the euro area needs further support and new measures.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. it is well known that the lack of financial resources caused by tax evasion and avoidance is offset by the additional financial burden on european citizens. this fact alone should be convincing enough to favour this motion for a resolution. the proposal also provides for an increase in corporate taxation and the promotion of crossborder cooperation between member states to combat tax evasion and avoidance.
the explanations of vote are closed. (the sitting was suspended at 1.35 p.m. and resumed at 3 p.m.)
i would like to thank the commissioner for his reply. china's organ procurement policy is inhuman and cruel. ngos accuse china of taking valuable organs from death row prisoners for the market, even against the will of the victims. it is estimated that about 3,000 people are sentenced to death in china each year. according to former chinese transplant doctors, the organs are also harvested from living people so that they can continue to circulate as long as possible. i'll spare you the details. the case of the falun gong faith community, whose followers are being targeted and persecuted, is also dramatic for me. they are thus made available to the market as organ donors against their will. these organ harvesting operations are shocking and contradict every notion of human dignity. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. it is good that you are addressing this issue today, and unfortunately you are only addressing it, because with a major trading partner like china, the eu is happy to refrain from taking any firm action. i hope that this time there will be an exception and that the union will take the same firm action against the great economic power china. (the speaker agrees to answer a question under the 'blue card' procedure under rule 149 (8) of the rules of procedure)
answer to a question on the 'blue card' procedure. thank you for asking, but i couldn't make out the real question. it was a co-authored paper by you, in which you endorse me. and if you ask the question, is there a market? yes, of course, obviously not everything is free, and of course there is a demand, there are many sick people, and i guess it's not going to be all voluntary and free. so naturally these organs are traded and passed on in a market. that's the answer.
i would like to thank the commissioner for his reply. the 26 years of civil war saw the most serious violations of human rights and the geneva convention. this on both sides. however, since 2009, the situation in sri lanka should have stabilized. the de facto rule of the separatist tamil north is over. the government is currently accused of numerous human rights violations - it is estimated that 30,000 people, including many journalists, have been killed or disappeared. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a decision on the matter. the european union must of course call on the government to clarify this and to stop human rights violations. the union will do the same. it is much easier to beat the small sri lanka on the table than, for example, the great power of china. i will, however, personally take a picture on the spot. i'm going to go to sri lanka, travel the country with my eyes open, make my own picture. i'm very optimistic about the future of this country.
